Five viscosity cases and seven interactions give 35 fluid realizations governed by a common autonomous system. When the intrinsic dark-energy pressure is reconstructed from the continuity equation, dark-energy viscosity leaves the expansion history unchanged. Interaction and dark-matter viscosity enter through their net contribution, producing further exact background degeneracies. Each realization admits stable de Sitter attractors in physical parameter domains, either dominated by dark energy or containing residual dark matter sustained by exchange and viscous stress. Representative posterior trajectories connect the inferred present states to these endpoints. Using supernovae, cosmic chronometers, DESI baryon acoustic oscillations and a compressed Planck distance prior, the density-product interaction yields a Hubble constant of $71.15^{+1.53}_{-1.64}$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$. Conditional on the applicability of that prior, the preferred transfer from dark energy to dark matter lowers the minimum chi-squared by 75.16 relative to noninteracting HHDE and reduces the discrepancy with the local distance-ladder measurement to approximately one standard deviation when both uncertainties are combined.

arxiv.org/abs/2509.06489.title: Optimal robust detection statistics for pulsar timing arrays
arxiv.org/abs/2509.06489.excerpt:
arXiv:2509.06489v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) seek to detect a nano-Hz stochastic gravitational-wave background (GWB) by searching for the characteristic Hellings and Downs angular pattern of timing residual correlations. So far, the evidence remains below the conventional $5\sigma$ threshold, as assessed using the literature-standard "optimal cross-correlation detection statistic". While this quadratic combination of cross-correlated data maximizes the deflection (signal-to-noise ratio), it does not maximize the detection probability at fixed false-alarm probability (FAP), and therefore is not Neyman-Pearson (NP) optimal for the assumed noise and signal models. The NP-optimal detection statistic is a different quadratic form, but is not used because it also incorporates autocorrelations, making it more susceptible to uncertainties in the modeling of pulsar timing noise. Here, we derive the best compromise: a quadratic detection statistic which is as close as possible to the NP-optimal detection statistic (minimizing the variance of its difference with the NP statistic) subject to the constraint that it only uses cross-correlations, so that it is less affected by pulsar noise modeling errors. We study the performance of this new NPMV statistic for a simulated PTA whose noise and (putative) signal match those of the NANOGrav 15-year data release: GWB amplitude $A_{\rm gw} = 2.1 \times 10^{-15}$ and spectral index $\gamma = 13/3$. Compared to the literature-standard "optimal" cross-correlation detection statistic, the NPMV statistic increases the detection probability by 47% when operating at a $5\sigma$ false-alarm probability of $\alpha = 2.9 \times 10^{-7}$.

arxiv.org/abs/2512.12155.title: AGN x-ray reflection spectroscopy with ML_MYTORUS: Neural posterior estimation with training on observation-driven parameter grids
arxiv.org/abs/2512.12155.excerpt:
arXiv:2512.12155v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: X-ray spectroscopy of active galactic nuclei (AGN) probes circumnuclear matter geometry. Many AGN show a narrow Fe K $\alpha$ line at 6.4 keV and associated Compton-scattered continua in their x-ray spectra, due to primary continuum scattering in cold, neutral material far from the central supermassive black hole. We present a novel approach via Simulation-Based Inference with Neural Posterior Estimation (SBI-NPE) and train a machine learning neural network (ML NN) model based on $NuSTAR$ spectral fitting results from the literature, employing the physically motivated MYTORUS-decoupled model, which distinguishes line-of-sight from global equivalent neutral hydrogen column density ($N_{\rm H,Z}$ vs. $N_{\rm H,S}$). To overcome the limitations of traditional frequentist fitting (e.g., lack of automation, reproducibility, computational cost), we implement normalizing flows and autoregressive networks to learn flexible posterior distributions from simulated spectra. From 34 $NuSTAR$ spectral fitting literature results, we simulate 34,000 spectra for both a uniform and a Gaussian parameter distribution. We train our neural network to determine four key MYTORUS parameters, $N_{H,Z}, N_{H,S}$, power-law spectral index $\Gamma$, and relative normalization $A_{\rm S}$. The observation-based grid significantly outperforms uniform sampling, achieving predictive accuracy for individual parameters >90% ($N_{H,S}$ and $A_{\rm S}$), 89% ($N_{\rm H,Z}$), and 82% ($\Gamma$) within $\pm1\sigma$. For all four parameters simultaneously, predictive accuracy remains high ($\sim$70%). The trained NN ML, ML_MYTORUS, is publicly available with a web interface for fast and reproducible parameter inference from $NuSTAR$ spectra. We illustrate its use via application to NGC 4388. This work shows that SBI offers great potential for future distant x-ray reflection studies in AGN or Galactic x-ray binary spectra.

arxiv.org/abs/2602.05955.title: Improved Heavy Dark Matter Annihilation Search from Dwarf Galaxies with HAWC
arxiv.org/abs/2602.05955.excerpt:
arXiv:2602.05955v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Understanding dark matter's elusive nature is crucial for the framework of particle physics and expanding the Standard Model. This analysis utilizes the High Altitude Water Cherenkov (HAWC) gamma ray Observatory to indirectly search for dark matter (DM) by studying gamma ray emission from dwarf spheroidal galaxies (dSphs). Selected for their high ratio of dark matter to baryonic matter, dSphs are useful for this type of search owing to the low background emission. In comparison to previous HAWC studies, we significantly improve our sensitivity to DM from dSphs due to improvements to our event reconstruction and reduced hadronic contamination. We expanded the number of dSphs studied, DM annihilation channels into the Standard Model (SM), and the amount of data collected on each previously studied dSph. We searched for DM signals in each dSph using the latest version of the algorithms used to reconstruct data from the primary detector of the HAWC instrument. We report that we do not detect evidence of DM from dSphs, so we place upper limits for the velocity-weighted DM annihilation cross-section ($\langle\sigma v \rangle$) on the order of $10^{-23}~\text{cm}^3\text{s}^{-1}$ for a DM mass range of $1-10^4$ TeV.

arxiv.org/abs/2604.07878.title: The deci-Hz gravitational wave signal from the collapse of rotating very massive stars
arxiv.org/abs/2604.07878.excerpt:
arXiv:2604.07878v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We calculate the gravitational wave signal from the collapse of a rotating 300 $M_\odot$ star just above the upper end of the pair-instability supernova regime. The large-scale asymmetries that develop during the collapse produce a strong signal in the deci-Hz range that has a characteristic shape that is likely amenable to a template-based search. Although tempered by the low incidence of nearby astrophysical candidates, the most ambitious designs for deci-Hz detectors could detect such signals out to distances of ~250 Mpc, possibly at a rate of 0.3 per year. Additional numerical modeling is required to refine these rate estimates, however. We also demonstrate that proposed deci-Hz GW observation missions, even without confident single-source detections, could be used to provide information about the population of astrophysical candidates and, in particular, constrain the initial mass function of very massive stars.

arxiv.org/abs/2604.11898.title: Beyond the Diffusion Coefficient: Propagators and Memory in Cosmic Ray Transport
arxiv.org/abs/2604.11898.excerpt:
arXiv:2604.11898v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Cosmic ray (CR) transport is usually modeled with a single diffusion coefficient, but this description captures only the growth of the variance. Distinct transport mechanisms can share the same effective diffusion coefficient while producing different particle distributions and approaches to the diffusive limit. The distinction matters in multiphase, structured and time-dependent media, and is reflected in the observed variation of CR transport near pulsar wind nebulae, supernova remnants and molecular clouds, and in particle-tracing studies that show both superdiffusion and subdiffusion. We therefore develop a propagator-based framework centered on the probability distribution of particle positions, or equivalently its Fourier-Laplace transform. This object is compact and complete for the observable spatial transport. It naturally reveals if large scale transport has memory: when the CR flux depends on earlier rather than just the instantaneous pressure gradient. Such memory arises when dynamically relevant transport states, such as trapping or phase changes, are not retained in the macroscopic description. Using the Montroll-Weiss formalism, we measure the propagator directly from trajectories, recover the associated memory kernel, and represent broad kernels with a Prony expansion. Applied to a multiphase medium, the framework shows that slow regions can regulate escape without dominating the total residence time budget. We also introduce an accelerated Monte Carlo method for coarse-grained transport, showing that if trapping structures evolve while particles are still sampling them, the static long-time limit need not be reached. This provides a foundation for observational applications, particle-tracing measurements and CR-MHD closures.

arxiv.org/abs/2604.14659.title: Constraining Quintessential Inflation with ACT: A Gauss-Bonnet Gateway
arxiv.org/abs/2604.14659.excerpt:
arXiv:2604.14659v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Recent results from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT), which, when combined with Planck, CMB lensing, DESI DR2 with BAO data, indicate a higher and more tightly constrained scalar spectral index, $
s = 0.9743 \pm 0.0034$ P-ACT-LB), place several inflationary models under tension, with quintessential inflation pushed close to or beyond the $2\sigma$ boundary in the $r$--$
s$ plane for this dataset combination. In this work, we revisit quintessential inflation within the framework of Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet (EGB) gravity, where a scalar field non-minimally coupled to the Gauss--Bonnet invariant modifies the inflationary dynamics. We consider three representative coupling functions -- exponential, hyperbolic secant, and hyperbolic tangent -- and show that the exponential and sech-type couplings can shift the predicted values of $r$ and $
s$ into the $1\sigma$ region allowed by the P-ACT-LB-BK18 combination, thereby restoring consistency with these observations. In contrast, the tanh-type coupling remains disfavoured, underscoring the sensitivity of inflationary observables to the coupling structure. We further investigate the reheating phase using a model-independent parameterisation and demonstrate that viable thermal histories can be realised even in the absence of a potential minimum, with reheating temperatures consistent with Big Bang nucleosynthesis bounds. We emphasise that the quantitative conclusions are conditional on the choice of dataset combination: the preference for a higher $
s$ is driven by the ACT data and, indirectly, by DESI BAO, whereas combinations based on Planck alone or including the latest SPT-3G data yield lower central values of $
s$ and correspondingly milder tension for standard quintessential inflation.

arxiv.org/abs/2604.16093.title: JWST and Keck observations of the off-nuclear tidal disruption event TDE 2025abcr: An evolving reprocessing layer
arxiv.org/abs/2604.16093.excerpt:
arXiv:2604.16093v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Off-nuclear tidal disruption events (TDEs) provide a rare probe of massive black holes (MBHs) outside galactic nuclei. Only a handful are known, including five X-ray-selected candidates and three optically selected events. We present observations of TDE 2025abcr, the second optically selected off-nuclear TDE, discovered at a projected offset of $9.08 \pm 0.02$ kpc from the nucleus of its host galaxy. We analyze X-ray, UV, optical, and infrared (IR) data from Swift, Keck, ZTF, and JWST. Broad H and He emission lines in the optical and IR confirm a TDE-H-He classification. From luminosity scaling relations and MOSFiT modeling, we infer a BH mass of $10^{6}$-$10^{7}\,M_{\odot}$, substantially smaller than the $10^{8.38 \pm 0.42}\,M_{\odot}$ BH inferred for the host-galaxy nucleus. We observe velocity evolution in the N III + He II emission complex, shifting from $-100$ km s$^{-1}$ at day $-7$ to $+1000$ km s$^{-1}$ by day $+29$, which we interpret as radiative transfer effects in an evolving reprocessing layer. The IR SED deviates from a thermal blackbody, with $\nu L_{\nu} \propto \lambda^{-2.13 \pm 0.04}$, significantly shallower than the Rayleigh-Jeans slope of $\lambda^{-3}$. We rule out dust as the source of this IR excess. Two possibilities remain: free-free emission from reprocessing gas, or an unresolved stellar cluster at the TDE location. Reprocessed emission provides a natural explanation for the IR excess but an underlying stellar cluster of mass $\log(M_{*}/M_{\odot}) = 7.57 \pm 0.02$ and age $<$2 Gyr is also consistent with the data. If interpreted as a stellar cluster, the inferred mass suggests a stripped remnant of a satellite galaxy. The wandering MBH most likely originated in a minor merger with a smaller galaxy, although dynamical ejection from the host nucleus cannot yet be ruled out.

arxiv.org/abs/2605.00659.title: The NIKA2 Cosmological Legacy Survey in COSMOS: Final 1.2mm and 2mm source catalogs and redshift distribution of dusty star-forming galaxies
arxiv.org/abs/2605.00659.excerpt:
arXiv:2605.00659v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present the final 1.2mm and 2mm source catalogs and the redshift distribution of the mm-selected population from the NIKA2 Cosmological Legacy Survey (N2CLS) in the COSMOS field. Our aim is to provide a comprehensive dataset for studying the physical properties and evolution of high-redshift DSFGs. N2CLS covers ~1070 arcmin2 with median noise levels of 315$\mu$Jy and 91$\mu$Jy at 1.2 and 2mm, respectively. Sources are extracted with a S/N threshold of 3.9, ensuring >80% purity. Multi-wavelength counterparts are identified using high-resolution interferometric (sub-)mm data (NOEMA, ALMA) and radio observations (VLA, MeerKAT). Redshifts are compiled from spectroscopic and photometric catalogs (e.g., COSMOSWeb). The N2CLS master catalog includes 323 sources detected at >80% purity, with 104 sources detected in both bands, 197 only at 1.2mm, and 22 only at 2mm. Multi-wavelength identifications are secured for ~89% of the sample. The redshift distribution of 1.2mm sources peaks at 2.8$\pm$0.1, consistent with the epoch of peak cosmic star formation. In the total sample, we lack redshift for ~2% of the identified galaxies, plus 34 sources for which no accurate positional proxy is available, preventing the identification of a multi-wavelength counterpart. We identify 66 galaxies at z>4. The observed redshift distribution agrees well with the SIDES simulations, while four other galaxy evolution models are statistically inconsistent with the data. N2CLS is the largest contiguous deep survey to date with this depth and homogeneous coverage. This homogeneous coverage is important, as 25% of N2CLS sources lack a SCUBA2 850 micron counterpart, likely because the strongly non-uniform noise distribution of the SCUBA2 map results in lower sensitivity in parts of the field. The released data products provide a legacy dataset for studying dust-obscured galaxy evolution.

arxiv.org/abs/2605.19040.title: IceCube Second Track Data Release IceTracks-DR2: Data from 2008-2022 for Neutrino Source Searches
arxiv.org/abs/2605.19040.excerpt:
arXiv:2605.19040v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present IceCube's latest release of muon track data for neutrino point-source searches, extending the previously published 10-year dataset to cover 14 years of observations (April 6, 2008 - May 23, 2022). This release features an updated event selection and improved detector calibration for data recorded after June 1, 2010. The release also includes binned instrument response functions and effective areas, enabling the community to perform sensitive searches for steady and transient neutrino sources. We report on key science results obtained with this dataset using internal IceCube analysis tools and compare them to those derived from analyses based on the binned response functions included in this public release. To facilitate reproducible research, we provide benchmark results obtained using this data release and publicly available software. This release represents IceCube's most sensitive and comprehensive publicly available all-sky muon track dataset to date and should be preferred over previous releases.

arxiv.org/abs/2605.24089.title: Exploring the Dark Sector: Interacting Radiation in Light of Modern Cosmological Probes
arxiv.org/abs/2605.24089.excerpt:
arXiv:2605.24089v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: [abridged] We constrain a phenomenological dark radiation (DR) framework consisting of free-streaming and fluid-like components, providing a model-independent extension of the standard radiation sector. Using Planck CMB data, DESI DR2 BAO measurements, and Pantheon+ and DES Y5 (Dovekie) supernova samples, we derive constraints on additional relativistic degrees of freedom and assess their impact on cosmological tensions. We obtain $N_{\rm fld}<0.66$ (95% C.L.) from CMB data alone, while the combination with BAO yields $N_{\rm fs}=2.93\pm0.23$ and $N_{\rm fld}=0.36^{+0.16}_{-0.21}$ (68% C.L.), consistent with Standard Model expectations for free-streaming radiation. The DR framework significantly alleviates the Hubble tension through an enhanced early-time expansion rate, which reduces the sound horizon scale. The tension with SH0ES is reduced from highly significant in $\Lambda$CDM to statistically non-significant for CMB+BAO data according to the $\mathcal{T}$-statistic. Bayesian model comparison shows no decisive preference for DR over $\Lambda$CDM when SH0ES is excluded, with results in the regime of weakly disfavoured. However, including SH0ES data leads to decisive Bayesian evidence in favour of the DR scenario. Overall, DR provides a compelling framework for resolving the Hubble tension. When CMB, BAO, Pantheon$+$ and SH0ES data are considered, we find an increased effective radiation content, $N_{\rm tot}=3.63^{+0.13}_{-0.15}$, with a fraction of free-streaming radiation, $f_{\rm fs}=0.392\pm 0.026$, a reduced sound horizon scale, $r_d = 141.8^{+1.3}_{-1.2}\,\mathrm{Mpc}$, and a higher primordial helium fraction, $Y_{\rm He}=0.2530 \pm 0.0017$, which lies at the level of approximately $\sim 2$-$2.5\sigma$ above direct determinations from metal-poor H II regions, while remaining broadly consistent with other abundance measurements within current uncertainties.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.30644.title: Testing the prevalence of hydrogen-silicate miscibility in young sub-Neptunes
arxiv.org/abs/2606.30644.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.30644v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Hydrogen-silicate miscibility can significantly alter the interior structure and thermal evolution of sub-Neptunes. We consider the interplay between this miscibility and stellar-driven atmospheric escape. We find that, for the first $\sim 100$ Myrs, sub-Neptunes store most of their hydrogen content within their miscible interiors, protecting it from escape. As hydrogen is removed from the top of the atmosphere, more hydrogen is exsolved from the miscible interior, resupplying the envelope mass and delaying the planet's contraction when compared with models that do not account for miscibility. We construct a population-level Bayesian hierarchical inference model which tests for the prevalence of fully miscible sub-Neptunes. With conservative measurement uncertainty and no completeness corrections, we predict that $\sim 100-200$ observed young sub-Neptunes with measured radii, masses and ages $\lesssim 1$ Gyr are required to differentiate between fully miscible and immiscible models. This survey size requirement decreases with improved measurement uncertainty. Furthermore, one can reliably infer the underlying distributions of planetary initial conditions if completeness corrections are included in the analysis.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.10403.title: The muon Moonshot: Moon subsurface tomography with upward-going muons
arxiv.org/abs/2607.10403.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.10403v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We propose a novel muon Moonshot concept for lunar subsurface tomography based on upward-going muons originating from the lunar regolith. Unlike Earth, the Moon lacks an atmosphere, leaving dense regolith below and a near-vacuum environment above. Consequently, most downward-going hadrons are absorbed before decaying, while upward-going hadrons escaping the regolith can decay in flight, producing a significant flux of lunar muons. These muons can be detected by instruments on the lunar surface or in near-lunar orbit. We perform Monte Carlo simulations to investigate their energy spectra, angular distributions, and integrated fluxes under various theoretical and detector configurations. The results indicate that the lunar muon flux is sensitive to detector altitude under idealized geometry. This dependence demonstrates its potential as a novel, non-invasive probe of shallow subsurface voids. We also present case studies on the detection of underground cavities and water resources. For shallow overburden, large cavity signals remain detectable with estimated backgrounds and systematics. Weaker water signals remain challenging. Potential implementations in future lunar missions are also discussed.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.17616.title: On the Separation Between the Brightest Cluster Galaxy and the Intracluster Light
arxiv.org/abs/2607.17616.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.17616v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present a model-based framework to define an aperture separation between the brightest cluster galaxy (BCG) and the intracluster light (ICL). Using the intrinsic BCG and ICL components predicted by the semi-analytic model \texttt{FEGA25}, we determine, for each halo, the aperture radius that minimizes the bias in the recovered ICL mass. The optimal radius is obtained by balancing the BCG stellar mass lying outside the aperture with the ICL mass enclosed within it. At $z=0$, the optimal aperture in physical units increases with halo mass approximately as $r_{\rm cut}\propto M_{\rm halo}^{0.28}$, close to the expected virial scaling. When expressed in units of the virial radius, the aperture becomes nearly independent of halo mass, with $r_{\rm cut}/R_{\rm vir}\simeq 0.045$ at $10^{14}M_\odot$. Applying the resulting aperture prescriptions, we recover the intrinsic BCG mass to better than 8\% (lowest percentile), while the ICL mass is recovered with median values very close to unity, and an average scatter of $\pm 3\%$. Extending the analysis to $z=1$ and $z=2$, we find that the mass trends remain similar, with the slope and intercept of $r_{\rm cut}/R_{\rm vir}$ that stay stable. Robustness tests show that the inferred aperture is most sensitive to the ICL concentration and BCG size, but the main trends are preserved. Our results provide a physically motivated aperture definition for connecting observational BCG--ICL measurements to intrinsic model components.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.19494.title: The silent dark sector: a field-theory approach to unified dark fluids with vanishing speed of sound
arxiv.org/abs/2607.19494.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.19494v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We introduce a novel class of field-theory models that provide a unified description of the dark sector as a single perfect fluid with vanishing sound speed. These models also admit the interpretation of cold dark matter interacting with vacuum energy while avoiding any phantom behavior and including standard $\Lambda$CDM as a particular case. Built upon a single scalar field invariant under transverse diffeomorphisms, the framework naturally implements the constraints imposed in the so called mimetic models. We analyze a particular simple example exhibiting an effectively evolving dark energy and find that it can reproduce the DESI best-fit CPL evolution with the same number of free parameters.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.23494.title: Hermes - Towards an Optimal High-Performance Algorithm for Cosmic Statistics of Large Data Sets
arxiv.org/abs/2607.23494.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.23494v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present Hermes, an in situ multiresolution framework for efficient and flexible measurements of cosmic large-scale-structure statistics from discrete catalogues. Hermes replaces conventional ex situ counting of particle tuples with algebraic operations among window-filtered continuous fields. A discrete point distribution is first reconstructed as a continuous density field in a compact scaling-function representation, in which two- and higher-point statistics are formulated as spatial products of locally filtered fields. This formulation expresses conventional binning for counts-in-cells and two- and higher-point correlation functions through window functions. Changing the window kernels defines generalised statistics without redesigning the estimator. We further introduce PyHermes, an open-source Python implementation of this framework, combining multiresolution field reconstruction with FFT-based window convolution, MPI/thread parallelism, and GPU acceleration for high-order field contractions. The framework supports a broad range of measurements, including isotropic and anisotropic two-point statistics, marked correlations, standard and multipole three-point functions, filtered statistics, and Fourier-space differential operators for constructing derived physical fields. Using halo catalogues from cosmological N-body simulations, we demonstrate PyHermes through a range of clustering statistics and use benchmarks to quantify its computational efficiency and scalability for large-scale data sets. By separating field representation from statistical windows, Hermes provides a unified computational framework in which a single reconstructed field can be reused for a wide range of standard and customised cosmic statistics. This field-window architecture enables scalable analysis of the large data sets expected from current and future galaxy surveys.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.24951.title: Gravitational Wave Modeling of White-Dwarf--Compact-Object Binaries and Observational Outlook
arxiv.org/abs/2607.24951.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.24951v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Binaries consisting of a white dwarf and a compact object (neutron stars, black holes, or sub-solar-mass compact objects) display unique orbital evolution and gravitational wave signals. We investigate the end stages of these systems by developing a novel integrator implementing mass transfer and 2.5-order Post-Newtonian kinematics. White-dwarf--compact-object binaries are subject to two phases: a slow inspiral during which binary evolution is dominated by weak-gravity radiation reaction and a quicker "outspiral" dominated by mass transfer. These systems have unique gravitational waveforms with several characteristic features including an accumulation of signal near the maximum cutoff frequency set by the transition between in- and outspiral. We investigate trends in gravitational wave parameters based on component masses. In particular, maximum cutoff frequency depends strongly on white dwarf mass and compactness. It is unlikely that extragalactic binaries will be measured by LISA or current or future terrestrial detectors. However, white-dwarf--compact-object binary end stages will be an important source for future decihertz detectors such as DECIGO and LGWA: The final inspiral of tens of white-dwarf--neutron-star binaries will be detected annually by LGWA, and millions of inspirals along with thousands of outspirals will be detected by DECIGO. The ultimate fates of these binaries are diverse and dependent upon the intricacies of angular momentum loss. In particular, we show that white dwarfs with partners of sufficiently low/high mass can end their lives in mergers, while white dwarfs do not enter contact with partners of intermediate mass. The highest frequencies produced by white-dwarf--compact-object binaries in our tests are 10--20 Hz--incapable of mimicking sub-solar-mass compact object signals in terrestrial detectors or explaining S251112cm-like signals.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.00242.title: Stellar mergers and chemical element mixing: implications for metamorphic stellar evolution in AGN disks
arxiv.org/abs/2608.00242.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.00242v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Chemical mixing during stellar mergers can significantly influence the subsequent evolution of the merger remnant. We perform a suite of three-dimensional hydrodynamical simulations of stellar mergers, each evolved for $\sim100$ stellar dynamical times until the remnant reaches a quasi-hydrostatic equilibrium. The simulations incorporate subgrid-scale diffusion models to capture the turbulent mixing of chemical elements. Starting with an idealized polytropic equation of state (EOS), we first identify the dominant mixing mechanisms and investigate how the merger outcome depends on the mass ratio, relative velocity, impact parameter, and stellar structure. We then extend our simulations to the context of stars embedded in active galactic nucleus (AGN) disks, using a realistic, composition-dependent EOS and AGN stellar models generated with the stellar evolution code MESA. We find that mergers with both younger metamorphic stars and H-rich accreting AGN stars can substantially rejuvenate old metamorphic stars through efficient core mixing after thermal relaxation. The merger remnants are nitrogen-enriched, with ${\rm N/O}\sim1$--3 and ${\rm N/C}\gtrsim5$, comparable to the abundances observed in the nebula surrounding SN~1987A. During subsequent stellar evolution, the remnants may converge onto the main sequence of isolated metamorphic AGN stars once they reach accretion--wind equilibrium. They may also deposit a significant amount of chemically enriched material into the AGN disk. This work provides a physical framework for connecting hydrodynamical stellar mergers with the long-term evolution of AGN stars and their observational and chemical signatures.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.03302.title: Electron transport in a radiation-dominated plasma Application to solar corona brightenings
arxiv.org/abs/2608.03302.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.03302v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Bremsstrahlung scattering of fast electrons on ions can be enhanced by the microwave radiation present in the solar corona. It can account for the electron diffusive transport along magnetic loops and high precipitation rates. This process can also dominate the transport of thermal electrons confined in such loops. The influence of stimulated Bremsstrahlung scattering on the electron transport is studied, with focus on the return current induced by the fast electron population trapped in magnetic loops. Overall, transport coefficients are reevaluated in the radiation-dominated plasma, characterized by the stimulated action of radiation on the Bremsstrahlung electron-ion collision, down to thermal velocities. We develop a theoretical framework for electron transport driven by a large bandwidth, bright low-frequency part of the photon spectrum and compute a set of radiation-enhanced transport coefficients. UV, XEUV and hard X-ray signals from flares, evidencing anomalous resistivity, thermal conduction inhibition and high precipitation rates of fast electrons, are reinterpreted. The anomalous resistivity due to stimulated Bremsstrahlung scattering is found to dominate the classical resistivity in flares. The runaway effect due to Coulomb collisions is suppressed. Thermal conduction is inhibited compared to the Spitzer conduction, in agreement with coronal seismology of slow-mode waves. Stimulated Bremsstrahlung scattering is found to be a key collisional process in flaring events. It can explain the above loop-top hard X-ray signal due to the fast electrons, and the measured electrical conductivity due to the thermal electrons. As a perspective, the corresponding transport coefficients can be used in radiation MHD codes. The radiation model could also be applied to stimulate large-angle electron scattering in the kinetic or hybrid models used to study the solar corona.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.05106.title: Constraining Lorentz invariance violation from the depth of air-shower maximum
arxiv.org/abs/2608.05106.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.05106v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Hypothetical Lorentz invariance violation (LIV) remains strongly constrained but has not been excluded as a possible manifestation of new high-energy physics. In subluminal photon-sector LIV, suppressed Bethe$\unicode{x2013}$Heitler pair production modifies the electromagnetic component of extensive air showers. We present a simulation-based toy analysis of this effect using published Pierre Auger fluorescence-detector distributions of the reconstructed depth of air-shower maximum. The modified distributions of the depth of the shower maximum are folded with the Auger detector-response parametrizations and compared with the data using free composition fractions in each reconstructed-energy bin. Within this approach, the comparison gives a sensitivity to LIV compatible with that expected from ultra-high-energy photon-induced showers. We obtain $M_{\rm LIV}\gtrsim 6.5\times 10^{18}\,\text{GeV}$ for the photon-sector LIV mass scale $M_{\rm LIV}$ ($95\%$ confidence level). This result should not be interpreted as a detector-level experimental limit because the detector response and reconstruction are simplified, and the result remains composition dependent. However, the approach presented here opens the way for constraining LIV in hadronic air showers with more detailed analyses.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.07288.title: Multi-dimensional NLTE radiative transfer for a double detonation Type Ia explosion model in the photospheric phase
arxiv.org/abs/2608.07288.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.07288v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Previous radiative transfer calculations have shown that both multi-dimensionality and NLTE (non local thermodynamic equilibrium) effects impact the synthetic observables predicted for Type Ia supernova explosion models. Here we carry out a 2D NLTE radiative transfer simulation in the photospheric phase for a double detonation model with a 1 M$_{\odot}$ carbon-oxygen core and 0.02 M$_{\odot}$ helium shell. The predicted observables demonstrate that departures from both spherical symmetry and local thermodynamic equilibrium are significant on scales relevant to comparisons with observations. The NLTE treatment leads to a bluer spectral energy distribution, more slowly declining optical-band light curves, changes to the near-infrared light curve shapes, and differences in the evolution of key spectral features. Although substantial viewing-angle variation is predicted for the model, the scale of the variation is not significantly impacted by NLTE effects up to peak. However, after peak, our 2D NLTE simulation retains a strong viewing-angle dependence in its spectra whereas our simulation of the same ejecta model using an approximate NLTE treatment predicts significantly reduced spectroscopic viewing-angle variation. The NLTE treatment leads to improved agreement with normal Type Ia supernovae, primarily due to the increased ionisation state of the simulation, although the absence of a secondary near-infrared maximum suggests that the ejecta remain over-ionised relative to observations after peak. Despite the improved agreement, many viewing angles still show excessive line blanketing, suggesting that the 0.02 M$_{\odot}$ helium-shell mass of the current model is too large to reproduce normal Type Ia supernovae over the majority of lines of sight.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.13321.title: JWST detects a dusty AGB-like source before the Type Ia-CSM supernova 2026sqf
arxiv.org/abs/2608.13321.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.13321v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Supernova (SN) 2026sqf recently appeared in the nearby face-on spiral galaxy NGC~3310 and has shown signs of strong interaction with a circumstellar medium (CSM). Such intense interaction, rare among nearby SNe, offers a valuable opportunity to reveal details on the origin and nature of its progenitor system. We analyzed the early-phase spectra and light curves (LCs) of SN 2026sqf. We identified a point source near the SN position in pre-explosion JWST and HST imaging, tested its association with the SN through astrometric alignment of pre- and post-explosion images and a chance-projection analysis, and constructed and modeled its spectral energy distribution (SED). The general characteristics of the spectra, the strengths of the emission lines, and the LC evolution all suggest that SN 2026sqf belongs to the rare SN Ia-CSM subclass, which would make it the closest known member (D~19 Mpc). The point source is a credible counterpart of the progenitor system, the first such identification for this SN subclass. Under our modeling assumptions, carbonaceous dust around a luminous evolved star provides a reasonable description of its combined SED; compared with local analogues, the candidate most closely resembles an extreme asymptotic giant branch (AGB) star. We report the first candidate pre-explosion counterpart of a thermonuclear SN identified in JWST imaging. Our results support the scenario in which SNe Ia-CSM emerge from a system consisting of a white dwarf and an evolved giant (probably AGB) star. Strong binary interaction, possibly involving common-envelope evolution or a merger, is a natural explanation for the observed properties of the SN and its candidate counterpart, though the channel and timescale remain uncertain. Late-time follow-up, especially with JWST, will test the identification and the conclusions of our early-phase analysis.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.17801.title: The high entropy of the UHECR arrival direction distribution favors a light composition
arxiv.org/abs/2608.17801.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.17801v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We analyze the constraints on the composition of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs), and on the density and distribution of their sources, that may be inferred from their arrival-direction distribution, using a novel semi-analytical description of the propagation energy loss of atomic nuclei ($A>4$) with energy $>2\times10^{19}~\text{eV}$, that allows generating UHECR arrival maps faster than by using detailed propagation simulations and yields insights to the impact of propagation energy loss. We show that the anisotropy of the UHECR arrival direction distribution due to the large-scale structure (LSS) of matter distribution is larger for heavy nuclei composition compared to protons, despite their larger deflections by magnetic fields, due to their shorter propagation distance and weaker dependence of rigidity on observed energy. Identifying the LSS anisotropy signal is hampered for heavy nuclei due to their large deflections by the uncertain Galactic magnetic field (GMF). We introduce a new measure of anisotropy, an "entropy" of the arrival-direction distribution, that is largely independent of the GMF configuration and has strong discriminating power between heavy- and light-composition models. Analyzing the public $>3.2\times10^{19}$~eV Auger data, we show that the correlation with the LSS on large angular scales is weak and requires a low source density, $s_0\le10^{-4}{\rm Mpc}^{-3}$, to allow masking the LSS signature by "cosmic-variance" ($s_0=10^{-2}{\rm Mpc}^{-3}$ is ruled out at $>99\%$ confidence level (CL)). The high entropy of the distribution is consistent with proton models and inconsistent with heavy nuclei models at $>96\%$ CL for $s_0\ge10^{-5}{\rm Mpc}^{-3}$. Reducing the absolute energy calibration uncertainty may allow detection of the LSS correlation for proton models (increased exposure alone will not suffice due to the dominance of cosmic variance).

arxiv.org/abs/2608.18334.title: PowerFull: fast and accurate computation of the relativistic angular galaxy power spectrum including local primordial non-Gaussianity
arxiv.org/abs/2608.18334.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.18334v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Current and forthcoming wide-field galaxy surveys, such as SPHEREx and Euclid, provide a unique opportunity to probe the ultra-large scales of structure formation, where primordial non-Gaussianity, often parameterized by $f_\text{NL}$, is expected to leave its most detectable imprint. At the same time, these surveys inevitably enter regimes where relativistic and wide-angle effects become significant, requiring careful modeling to extract unbiased cosmological information. We address these challenges by applying the total-angular-momentum (TAM) formalism to describe redshift-space clustering beyond the flat-sky approximation. The standard Fourier-mode description, which characterizes distortions by the angle between a mode and a line of sight, becomes ill-defined over wide fields, whereas the TAM basis naturally separates radial and angular contributions and incorporates the relevant relativistic effects. Within this framework, we provide a new parameterization of wide-angle predictions that can be compared directly with survey data. We then introduce PowerFull, a modification of the Julia-based 2-FAST package, which enables efficient computation of the full relativistic angular power spectrum. Finally, using Fisher information matrix-based analyses, we show that a survey like SPHEREx reaches $\sigma(f_\text{NL}) \sim 1$, but that neglecting the relativistic and wide-angle contributions shifts the recovered $f_\text{NL}$ by an amount of order its own uncertainty: at this precision the inferred value is biased unless the clustering is modeled consistently.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.24459.title: Wideband overlapped polyphase channelizer for kinetic inductance detector readout: split-path architecture and experimental characterization
arxiv.org/abs/2608.24459.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.24459v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Frequency-multiplexed readout of kinetic inductance detector arrays measures the complex transmission of thousands of superconducting resonators. The channelizer that separates them introduces systematic effects: a gain that depends on where each tone falls in the channel grid, leakage between channels and added noise. This article presents a 4096-channel polyphase channelizer with 2/1 overlap for a 4.096 GS/s input, implemented on a first-generation radio-frequency system-on-chip, and a procedure to characterize it on the board with two receive chains, one digitizing the excitation as a reference. A split-path architecture computes the two overlap states in parallel filter branches at 256 MHz and reorders them frame by frame, under three control rules; it keeps only the transform stage at 512 MHz and affords a prototype of 16 taps per polyphase path (65536 coefficients) at the multiplication rate of a published 8-tap bank. Each selected channel is exported as a complex series at 1 MS/s. The measured channel response follows the coefficient-table model within 0.15 dB down to -28 dB, with both overlapping channels at full gain across their common band. Leakage into every measured channel 1.875 MHz or more from the tone is -94 dBc or lower, apart from images attributed to converter interleaving. The signal-to-noise ratio per sample lies within 1.7 dB of the limit set by the data-sheet noise density of the converter, and an emulated detector pulse is recovered with a decay time of 14.65 $\mu$s (standard uncertainty 0.04 $\mu$s), within 0.7% of the expected value.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.26348.title: COSMOS-Web: From early star-formation enhancement to late suppression in galaxy groups
arxiv.org/abs/2608.26348.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.26348v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Galaxy groups trace dense environments where interactions, gas removal, and reduced accretion may drive quenching. Common diagnostics trace star formation only over short timescales ($\lesssim100$ Myr), so time-resolved star formation histories (SFHs) are needed to separate recent changes from longer-term evolution at fixed mass and redshift. Using COSMOS-Web data, we test how group environment correlates with star-formation activity, and how this evolves with cosmic time and group-centric distance. We combine COSMOS2025/COSMOS-Web stellar masses and non-parametric SFHs with group detections and probabilistic memberships from AMICO. We compare stacked SFHs of group and field galaxies matched in mass and redshift, using the 30 richest groups in each redshift bin to measure how the SFH offset evolves with group-centric distance. Massive galaxies ($\log(M_\star/M_\odot)>10.5$) show the largest offsets but are already quenched in both environments. For lower masses ($8.1<\log(M_\star/M_\odot)<10.5$), suppression is clearest at $z<1$ (recent deficits of up to $0.7$ dex), while at $z>1$ SFHs show weaker suppression or occasional enhancement. The radial signal evolves similarly: quenching is broad across radius at low $z$, the inner--outer contrast appears at $z>0.5$, and any ordering at $z\gtrsim2$ remains tentative given growing uncertainties in the AMICO centroids. Groups are thus more mixed at early epochs, with both suppressed and occasionally elevated SFHs, while suppression dominates at $z<1$, most clearly for low-to-intermediate-mass galaxies. This fits a picture where inner-region galaxies spend more time in the group potential, undergo more passages through dense intra-group gas, and accrete less pristine cold gas, making quenching progressively clearer with cosmic time.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.27830.title: A Unified Tracer Analysis of DESI DR2 Baryon Acoustic Oscillations
arxiv.org/abs/2608.27830.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.27830v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We improve upon previous efforts to optimally combine overlapping galaxy samples in the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) analysis. By weighting each galaxy by its linear bias, overlapping galaxies are combined into a single, unified catalog, naturally avoiding double counting of cosmic volume and including all auto- and cross- information at the catalog level. Improvements over the previous effort include the addition of quasars out to $z=1.6$ to account for all overlapping DR2 tracers and redshift-dependent bias treatment to improve reconstruction. We report distance measurements using this unified tracer, and find them to be highly consistent with the baseline DR2 BAO analysis. We also test for tracer-dependent systematics within the DESI data, and find no evidence of tracer-dependent systematics within $0.8<1.6$. Finally, we take advantage of the unified tracer to rebin the analysis in redshift in order to more finely resolve the redshift-to-distance relation. Dynamical dark energy results on this finer redshift binning indicate that there is no missed feature in the expansion history in the redshifts $0.8<1.6$, and reproduces DESI's preference for an evolving dark energy equation of state.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.28975.title: Little Red Dots as Shock-Powered High-Energy Neutrino Sources
arxiv.org/abs/2608.28975.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.28975v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Little Red Dots (LRDs) are compact, high-redshift sources whose physical nature remains uncertain. Their optical spectra motivate a scenario in which their emission may be powered by shocks interacting with dense surrounding material. We investigate whether such interactions can power LRDs and contribute to the diffuse high-energy neutrino intensity measured by IceCube. In our simplified model, a fast central-engine outflow drives a shock through stationary or slow outflowing material, followed by a prescribed quasi-stationary interaction near the LRD photosphere. We consider the time-averaged neutrino emission from shock-active LRDs without requiring a single shock to persist throughout the LRD lifetime. We explore parameter ranges motivated by the observed and inferred properties of LRDs, finding solutions with shock luminosities 2.0e43 < L_s < 3.5e44 erg/s. Using an analytical framework for cosmic-ray acceleration and hadronic interactions in dense shock environments, we calculate the resulting high-energy neutrino emission and integrate it over the cosmological LRD population. For our fiducial cosmic-ray parameters, the average predicted contribution below 2e5 GeV increases from 0.2% for the lowest-luminosity quintile to 2% for the highest-luminosity quintile, while an illustrative higher-efficiency case reaches 13% of the IceCube diffuse neutrino intensity. These estimates assume all observed LRDs are shock-active. A smaller active fraction or a reduced covering factor would decrease the predicted intensity, whereas survey incompleteness could increase it. Improved models and population synthesis are needed to constrain the total LRD contribution.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.28057.title: A Diagnostic Method for Proto-Neutron Star Magnetic Fields by Supernova Fallback Neutrinos
arxiv.org/abs/2609.28057.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.28057v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Young isolated neutron stars exhibit a wide range of magnetic field strengths. To understand the origin of this diversity, it is important to observationally constrain magnetic fields during the proto-neutron star (PNS) phase. We propose a novel diagnostic of PNS magnetic fields using neutrinos associated with supernova fallback. By performing one-dimensional general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations of the supernova fallback onto a magnetized PNS, we investigate how the energy spectra of the fallback neutrinos depend on the PNS magnetic field strength and the fallback accretion rate. We find that stronger magnetic fields and lower accretion rates produce softer spectra because the fallback neutrinos are emitted mainly near the magnetospheric radius, which becomes larger under these conditions. To quantify this spectral softening, we define a hardness ratio based on event rates above and below 30 MeV and introduce a hardness-event-rate diagram. Using this diagram, we identify the parameter region in which our diagnostic is applicable. Its applicability depends on the PNS magnetic field strength, fallback accretion rate, onset time of the fallback phase, and neutrino mass ordering. We also investigate the dependence on the PNS radius and find that a larger radius produces softer spectra, indicating a degeneracy between the magnetic field and PNS compactness. An independent constraint on the PNS compactness would therefore enable us to better constrain the magnetic field. These results suggest that future multimessenger observations of galactic supernovae can provide a new window into the NS diversity.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.04081.title: AEGIS: Differentiable Mars Climate Model with Neural Closures
arxiv.org/abs/2610.04081.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.04081v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: General circulation models (GCMs) are the primary tool for simulating planetary atmospheres. They play a vital role in understanding Mars's atmosphere, as forecasting its unique weather is mission-critical for operations such as entry, descent, and landing. Mars poses unusual challenges for these models, as observations are sparse compared to Earth. In addition, a thin $CO_2$ atmosphere alongside a radiatively active dust cycle creates a volatile atmosphere with large diurnal temperature swings and no true terrestrial analog for validation. Existing Mars GCMs, including the LMD PCM, the NASA Ames Mars GCM, and PlanetWRF, are mature and physically detailed but are implemented in legacy Fortran with finite-difference or finite-volume solvers, and they do not expose gradients for calibration or machine learning. Here we present AEGIS, a modular differentiable Mars climate model that couples Mars's unique atmospheric physics to the Dinosaur dynamical core, with interfaces for neural closures. We showcase stable ten-Mars-year simulations that reproduce the seasonal $CO_2$ cycle while conserving the total $CO_2$ inventory, capture realistic large-scale surface-temperature structure, and produce surface pressure that follows Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA) topography. Gradients through coupled trajectories agree with finite differences and support physical calibration and neural training. We compare with conventional GCMs, highlighting the framework's computational efficiency and differentiability.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.04586.title: Revisiting damping of Alfv\'en waves in partially ionized plasmas
arxiv.org/abs/2610.04586.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.04586v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We investigate the damping rate of Alfv\'en waves by means of the linear analysis of the two-fluid ten-moments system. To treat effects of viscosity in a wide frequency range, we take account of the time evolution of the traceless part of the pressure tensor. In addition, to treat effects of viscosity in a wide range of the ionization degree, we consider interactions between hydrogen atoms and between protons and hydrogen atoms in the equation of the traceless part of the pressure tensor. We find approximate analytical solutions to the dispersion relation for some limits. Our analysis in the low-frequency limit shows that the viscous damping dominates over the frictional damping in the high-beta plasma, which is independent of the ionization degree. Therefore, the viscosity of hydrogen gas significantly affects cosmic-ray propagation in a partially ionized high-beta plasma.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.09477.title: Polarised X-ray emission from the accreting millisecond pulsar SAX J1808.4-3658 during an X-ray outburst and a type-I X-ray burst
arxiv.org/abs/2610.09477.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.09477v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Modelling the X-ray pulse profiles of accreting millisecond pulsars (AMSPs) is a key technique for constraining the masses and radii of neutron stars. To this end, measuring the properties of polarised X-rays provides crucial information on the system geometry. We present the significant detection by IXPE of linearly polarised 2-8 keV X-rays during the decay of the 2025 outburst of the 2.5 ms AMSP SAX J1808.4-3658, with an average polarisation degree of $2.9\%\pm0.5\%$ and a polarisation angle of $46{\deg}\pm5{\deg}$ (measured East of celestial North), offset by $\sim 16{\deg}$-$24{\deg}$ from the average direction observed in the optical band over various epochs during the main part of the outburst. The observed degree of X-ray polarisation is similar to that found in the only other source of this class that has been targeted so far. By using a pulse-phase timing solution obtained with IXPE and NuSTAR, which confirms the long-term evolution of the pulsar spin and orbit, we did not find any significant pulse phase-resolved variability in the normalised Stokes parameters. Interpreting the polarised X-rays as originating from hot spots on the NS surface indicates they are almost aligned with the spin axis. We also report an indication for linearly polarised emission with a degree of $16\%\pm6\%$ (2-6 keV) during the peak of a type-I thermonuclear X-ray burst, with an angle almost orthogonal to that of the persistent emission. If confirmed, this level would exceed expectations for X-rays reflected by a thin accretion disc.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.22338.title: Identifying deformed exoplanets with JWST and Ariel: A target selection metric for phase curve observations
arxiv.org/abs/2610.22338.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.22338v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The shape of an exoplanet encodes fundamental information about its internal structure. For close-in giant planets, strong stellar tidal forces induce measurable deformations that can be probed through high-precision photometry. These deformations are quantified by the fluid Love numbers, which characterise a planet's response to external perturbations and are directly linked to its internal density distribution. In this work, we assess the potential of JWST and the future Ariel mission to constrain the Love numbers of hot Jupiters through full-orbit phase curve observations. To identify the most promising targets for this science case, we introduce a new detection metric, the deformation metric (D), which combines the expected deformation amplitude with the anticipated photometric signal-to-noise ratio. We apply this metric to the Ariel target list and identify WASP-33 b, WASP-76 b, and HAT-P-32 b as the three most favourable targets that currently lack Love number measurements. Using WASP-76 b as a benchmark case, we perform end-to-end retrieval simulations and show that a single continuous JWST phase curve observation can constrain the Love number $h_{2f}$ to a precision of $\sigma_{h_2f} \approx 0.09$, while a single Ariel visit could achieve $\sigma_{h_{2f}} \approx 0.18$. Such precision is likely sufficient for Love number measurements to provide meaningful constraints on planetary interior models and to distinguish between competing interior-structure scenarios, opening a new observational avenue for probing the deep interiors of exoplanets.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.26434.title: The accretion flow and jet of M87: broadband modelling across spatial scales
arxiv.org/abs/2610.26434.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.26434v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The nearby radio galaxy M87 is an ideal laboratory for studying accretion flows and relativistic jet emission. The EHT collaboration conducted the most comprehensive multi-wavelength observational campaign of M87, in which radio instruments with resolutions ranging from tens of microarcseconds to about an arcsecond sampled different portions of the outflow. We model these data using a radiatively inefficient accretion flow (RIAF) with winds and a new multi-zone jet model, initially magnetically dominated, in which we solve the transport equation for the non-thermal electrons as they are injected, advected, and cooled along the jet. We then compare each radio flux with the jet emission within an effective aperture set by the angular scale of the corresponding observation and obtain the best fit for the jet parameters. The comparison across spatial scales favours a scenario in which the RIAF, rather than the jet, produces the compact $230~{\rm GHz}$ emission, while the jet dominates the lower-frequency radio, optical/UV and X-ray emission. The Jet+RIAF model connects the Bondi-scale gas supply to an accretion rate at the horizon of ${\approx}10^{-5}$ of the Eddington rate, consistent with EHT polarimetry, and the two jets carry in total ${\approx}13$ per cent of the accretion power, $10^{43}~{\rm erg~s}^{-1}$. The framework presented in this work provides a simple way to disentangle the accretion-flow and jet contributions to the emission from nearby radio galaxies.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.29006.title: Rotation in the Lagoon Nebula with K2
arxiv.org/abs/2610.29006.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.29006v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: A low-mass star's rotation rate drives its magnetic field, and in the case of young stars, also affects accretion and planetary formation. Observations of the rotation rates of young stars help constrain models of star and planet formation. We present rotation rates from K2 observations of stars in the ~1-2 Myr Lagoon Nebula, one of the youngest clusters with space-based rotation rates available. From 414 light curves we obtain reliable rotation periods for 325 stars; 124 of them are disk-bearing and 201 are disk-free. This constitutes a significant increase in the collection of K2 rotation rates available for ~1-5 Myr stars. The overall distribution is broadly consistent with expectations, in that the slowest rotators are mid-K and both lower and higher masses are on average faster rotating. There is weak evidence that disked stars rotate more slowly. There are a few complex periodic variables, but they appear to be surprisingly high mass compared to prior known examples of this kind of object.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.31545.title: SpecLess: A Multi Survey Python Package for Machine Learning Classification of Galaxy Morphology and Activity from Photometry
arxiv.org/abs/2610.31545.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.31545v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Galaxy morphology and spectroscopic activity are fundamental observational diagnostics of galaxy formation and evolution. However, the extent to which these properties can be recovered from broadband photometry and preserved across different sky surveys remains an important question. In this study, we use photometric data from KiDS+VIKING, the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys and SDSS+AllWISE to systematically investigate the complementary information provided by optical, near-infrared and mid-infrared wavelengths for galaxy classification. Our machine learning models achieve macro F1 scores of 0.9237 and 0.7398 for morphological and activity classification, respectively. We show that the contribution of near-infrared photometry varies across galaxy populations, yielding an improvement of 9.25 percentage points in the classification accuracy of red spiral galaxies. Controlled experiments on 5,235 galaxies common to KiDS+VIKING and DESI demonstrate that mid-infrared photometry provides greater complementary information for discriminating spectroscopic activity classes than additional optical measurements. Furthermore, cross-survey transfer experiments conducted on identical galaxies with fixed reference labels reveal direction-dependent performance losses in the generalizability of photometric classifiers. These findings demonstrate that the limitations of photometric galaxy classification are governed not only by the choice of algorithm but also by the physical properties of galaxy populations, wavelength coverage and catalogue-specific observational differences. As an outcome of this study, we present SpecLess, an open-source Python package providing survey-specific classifiers that require no spectroscopic information at inference.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.36209.title: DUETS: Red giant asteroseismic binaries. Binary confirmation and prospects for double-seismic model inference
arxiv.org/abs/2610.36209.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.36209v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Red giants displaying solar-like oscillations allow precise stellar properties to be derived. Asteroseismic binaries (ABs), which are gravitationally bound systems where both stars show detectable oscillations, can provide constraints on the interior of two coeval stars, allowing us to model them jointly and potentially obtain constraints unavailable from either star individually. This makes ABs potential laboratories for calibrating stellar evolution theory. In this context, AB candidates (ABCs) are systems showing two oscillators, which are as of yet not confirmed as gravitationally bound. We aimed to confirm ABCs and other red giant binary candidates, as well as demonstrate the advantages of AB modeling inference. We obtained spectroscopic indicators of binarity for 60 oscillating red giants that have photometric (33 stars) and/or asteroseismic (38) indications of binarity. We confirm 12 of our 60 targets as spectroscopic binaries, 8 of which are ABs as well. Cross-matching with Gaia DR3 and APOGEE DR17, we identify a further 9 likely binaries, at least 6 of which are also ABCs. We then investigated the impact of simultaneously modeling the oscillation modes of both oscillators of an AB. We inferred stellar properties for; one binary of extra-Galactic origin containing one detectable red-giant-branch (RGB) oscillator; one AB with RGB oscillators; and two ABCs with RGB oscillators. We find that the mode frequencies of the two ABCs and the confirmed AB are well-described with a coeval modeling of the stellar components. We demonstrate that the simultaneous modeling of ABs with two RGB stars can be used to infer the stellar helium content down to $3\%$ precision, compared to $5\%$ when using only the brightest star. Finally, the metal-poor binary KIC2971380 hints for a need to correct the $\nu_{max}$ scaling relation, supporting recent studies of extremely metal-poor oscillators.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.03019.title: Are habitable-zone TESS Objects of Interest really there? Period resolution from the full archive
arxiv.org/abs/2611.03019.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.03019v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: TESS Objects of Interest (TOIs) seen as single or duo transits carry a catalogue period that is undefined or equal to the separation of the two events, and their insolation and any habitable-zone label inherit it. We reanalyse all 187 TOIs catalogued with P = 0 or P >= 200 d using all public TESS data through Sector 107, with a flux-based method that weights each alias by per-epoch transit likelihoods, the transit duration and a geometric prior, and tests for coherence, data edges, contamination by other planets and instrumental artefacts. It recovers 12 published periods blindly and, in injection-recovery tests, 71 per cent of periods constrained by a new transit, with no wrong period. It resolves 28 periods and fixes 8 more by exclusion. Are habitable-zone TOIs really there? Mostly not: of the 28 duo-transits that a catalogue-period criterion places in the conservative habitable zone, about two are expected to lie there, both giant planets, and none of the 12 small (Rp < 4 Earth radii) ones; those resolved are aliases of hotter planets. Conversely, habitable-zone planets hide behind missing or wrong periods: we recover three published M-dwarf examples and validate TOI-2298 b, a 3.0 Earth-radius sub-Neptune at 146.58 d in the conservative habitable zone of a K dwarf. Of three further planets validated with new periods, TOI-6075 b (1.7 Earth radii, 416.5 d, 833 d not excluded) lies beyond the outer edge and is the second validated transiting planet smaller than 2 Earth radii with P > 1 yr. We release alias-marginalised habitable-zone probabilities for the whole sample.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.05504.title: Gravitational waves flooding the Universe after wall domination
arxiv.org/abs/2611.05504.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.05504v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We discuss a possible early Universe scenario, where radiation era is interrupted by the epoch of domination of domain walls eventually annihilating into particles. During this period the Universe undergoes accelerated expansion, while the comoving correlation length of the domain wall network remains constant. The network serves as a source of tensor modes, which get frozen upon exiting the horizon similarly to the case of inflationary fluctuations. The modes re-enter the horizon during the subsequent stage of radiation domination and since then contribute to the gravitational wave background. The period of wall domination is manifested in the spectral shape of gravitational waves via a distinctive plateau replacing a peak, which is characteristic for the scenario with sub-dominant walls. The gravitational waves are strong enough to be observed with present-day and future facilities in a broad range of frequencies. In particular, their energy density is sufficient to produce a significant impact on the effective number of neutrino species, unless the duration of wall domination is suitably constrained.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.07839.title: Multilayer magnetic structure toward NGC 1333 revealed by a square-degree optical polarimetric survey
arxiv.org/abs/2611.07839.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.07839v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Magnetic-field studies of star-forming regions are complicated by overlapping structures along the line of sight. We investigate the large-scale magnetic field toward NGC~1333 in Perseus, accounting for foreground polarization through stellar distances and optical polarimetry.
  Our wide-field $R$-band survey covers nearly one square degree and provides polarization measurements for approximately 840 stars, with distances from Gaia DR3 and StarHorse. We used polarization-distance trends and Stokes parameters to identify line-of-sight components and estimate foreground polarization. After subtracting it in Stokes space, we characterized the field using circular statistics and the angular dispersion function (ADF), comparing it with molecular-line and complementary polarimetric observations.
  The data reveal a polarized foreground at 160-300 pc and a cloud component beyond 300 pc. After correction, the plane-of-sky field rotates smoothly from $126.3\deg\pm0.8\deg$ in the northwest to $162.2\deg\pm0.6\deg$ in the southeast, remaining well ordered in both regions. The ADF gives turbulent-to-ordered field ratios of $0.054^{+0.025}_{-0.022}$ and $0.095^{+0.021}_{-0.047}$, corresponding to plane-of-sky strengths of $59^{+44}_{-23}$ and $46^{+50}_{-13}~\mu\mathrm{G}$. Residual foreground fluctuations may affect these estimates. CO data show multiple velocity components with spatially varying contributions. Corrected optical polarization agrees with the large-scale orientation traced by Planck, while near-infrared and JCMT/POL-2 data reveal localized deviations in denser structures.
  Our results indicate a coherent cloud-scale magnetic field with a smoothly changing orientation, alongside localized variations in dense structures. They demonstrate the value of combining stellar distances and wide-field optical polarimetry to disentangle foreground contributions.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13729.title: Angular momentum transport in a newborn protostar--disc system: magnetic braking, spiral arms and the magneto-rotational instability
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13729.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13729v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Angular momentum transport in young protostar--disc systems involves magnetic braking, magneto-rotational turbulence and gravitational instability, mechanisms that are usually studied separately and on different scales. We present a three-dimensional non-ideal magnetohydrodynamic simulation, including Ohmic and ambipolar diffusion, that follows the collapse of a $1~M_\odot$ dense core continuously from the cloud scale to the formation of the protostar, and then the resulting protostar--disc system for $\sim 64~\mathrm{yr}$ at a resolution of $\sim 10^{-4}~\mathrm{AU}$ at the protostellar surface. We decompose the azimuthally averaged angular momentum budget into Reynolds, Maxwell and gravitational torques, each split into a radial and a meridional component, over a quasi-steady phase of the evolution. The collapse produces a thick disc an order of magnitude more massive than the protostar, whose specific angular momentum decreases as it accretes. Accretion through the disc is vertically layered, with accreting and decreting layers at the same radius, a pattern set layer by layer by the torques. The transport separates into three regimes delimited by the coupling of the magnetic field to the gas. Magnetic braking operates in the envelope. Maxwell stresses dominate inside $\sim 0.1~\mathrm{AU}$, where the field recouples and the magneto-rotational instability develops. In the ambipolar dead zone that makes up the bulk of the disc, the Reynolds stress dominates, carried by $m=2$ spiral arms in a marginally unstable disc, with the gravitational stress as a secondary contributor. Meridional transport is as important as radial transport, so that a one-dimensional viscous model fitted to the net mass flux would require a negative $\alpha$ over part of the disc.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.14330.title: Linking Outer Solar System Objects in Archival DECam Imaging: A Multi-year Linker Tested on Held-out Known Objects, and 189 Multi-opposition Candidates Including Five L4 Neptune Trojans, Two Retrograde Objects and Eight with a > 150 au
arxiv.org/abs/2611.14330.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.14330v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: I link single-night detections in public DECam imaging: 74% of the NOIRLab Source Catalog DR2 (2012-2019) sky with four or more nights, and my extraction from 149,421 exposures (2020-2026). Of 931 secure known objects, single-season linking recovers 22.1-25.0%, a multi-year linker 26.5%, together 36.2%. The multi-year rule, fixed before its held-out tests, recovers 68% of DES objects brighter than r = 23.5 in a strip of its footprint and 14 of 47 known objects outside it. Its shifted-sky controls, complete for 162 of 165 blocks, return no candidate. For its 34 candidates not already known this limits pure chance alignments to under 4% (11% at seven nights), but not links that mix real and chance detections. At six nights real and control counts are indistinguishable. Identification by orbit finds 14 designated objects that a position check missed. The catalogue has 189 undesignated candidates with orbits from two or more oppositions, whose linked detections were re-measured on the images; 41 were then detected on two or more nights that their fits did not use. Listed apart are 63 weaker entries and 19 designated objects, 12 of them Rubin discoveries with 4.9-13.2 yr of earlier arc. Five are candidate L4 Neptune Trojans whose orbits and clones librate for 10 Myr (one reported independently by Jongma 2026, mostly from other data), two are retrograde candidates and eight have a > 150 au. There is no follow-up and no selection function. The Minor Planet Center has astrometry of 37 objects; unreleased positions are available on request, in confidence.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.15907.title: $uvby-\beta$ photoelectric photometry of FGK-type pulsating star candidates in the Kepler field: observations, stellar parameters and asteroseismic analysis
arxiv.org/abs/2611.15907.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.15907v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present $uvby-\beta$ photoelectric photometry of 218 FGK-type stars brighter than $Kp = 12$ mag in the Kepler field. Interstellar reddening was estimated using the observed photometric indices, distances from Gaia DR3, and the Bayestar19 three-dimensional dust maps. The sample was classified into dwarf and giant stars, and their metallicities and effective temperatures were determined using empirical photometric calibrations. The resulting parameters were compared with those reported in previous photometric and spectroscopic studies. We also analyzed the Kepler long-cadence light curves of the sample and determined the global asteroseismic parameters, including the frequency of maximum oscillation power ($\nu_{\max}$) and the large frequency separation ($\Delta\nu$), for red giants exhibiting solar-like oscillations. Finally, we performed a Bayesian isochrone-fitting analysis using PARSEC stellar evolutionary models, incorporating the photometric metallicities and effective temperatures, the asteroseismic parameters, and absolute visual magnitudes derived from Gaia DR3 data as observational constraints. This analysis provides estimates of the fundamental stellar parameters, including effective temperatures, metallicities, surface gravities, masses, and radii, together with their associated uncertainties.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.18876.title: Searching for Anisotropic Cosmic Birefringence with SPT-3G
arxiv.org/abs/2611.18876.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.18876v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We search for anisotropic cosmic birefringence using two years of data from the SPT-3G instrument on the South Pole Telescope. Anisotropic cosmic birefringence refers to a theorized dependence of the refractive index of the vacuum on the polarization of light that varies across the Universe in a statistically isotropic manner. Such an effect would manifest as a direction-dependent mixing of the $E$ and $B$ polarization modes of the cosmic microwave background (CMB), caused by rotation of the polarization angle as photons travel from the CMB last scattering surface to us. We present a measurement of the power spectrum of the rotation angle $\alpha$ in six bins across the angular multipole range $20 < L < 2048$, finding no evidence for cosmic birefringence with the spectrum consistent with zero. At 95% confidence, we set a new best upper limit on the amplitude of a scale-invariant birefringence power spectrum of $A_{\rm CB}<0.027$. Additionally, we place upper limits on a scale-dependent white noise model. We translate the scale-invariant upper limit to constraints on the axion coupling constant and primordial magnetic field strength, finding 95% confidence limits of $g_{\alpha\gamma} < 1.7\times 10^{-2}/H_I$ and $B_{\rm 1\,Mpc} < 9.6\,{\rm nG}$ respectively. We expect these limits to improve several-fold with the complete SPT-3G survey.

arxiv.org/abs/2505.01492.title: Photo- and Hadrodisintegration constraints on massive relics decaying into neutrinos
arxiv.org/abs/2505.01492.excerpt:
arXiv:2505.01492v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We perform a detailed study of the cosmological constraints on the decay of a relic particle $\phi$ into neutrinos, $\phi \rightarrow \nu \bar{\nu}$, in particular those arising from the observed light-element abundances in the early Universe. We focus on the late-time disintegration of the light elements previously synthesised during BBN. Several processes are relevant, including final-state radiation associated with the decay, as well as subsequent interactions of the injected neutrinos with the thermal background neutrinos or between themselves. All processes generically contribute to the production of electromagnetic and often also hadronic material and may therefore induce late-time photodisintegration and hadrodisintegration reactions, i.e.~the destruction of light elements that have previously been formed during BBN. Here, we examine this scenario with a Monte-Carlo inspired probabilistic approach rather than Boltzmann techniques, taking into account all of these different reactions as well as their interplay. We find the resulting constraints to be very significant, covering a broad range of previously unexplored masses and lifetimes of the relic source particle.

arxiv.org/abs/2511.10731.title: Keeping It Renormalizable: Minimal Baryogenesis induced Asymmetric Dark Matter
arxiv.org/abs/2511.10731.excerpt:
arXiv:2511.10731v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Many asymmetric dark matter scenarios have been proposed to date. Among them, perhaps the most motivated ones are those in which the dark matter asymmetry is induced from the baryon/lepton asymmetries via chemical equilibration without any new sources of CP violation. However, most of the models put forward along these lines have been excluded by now and/or are based on complicated setups. In this letter, we present a new, simple, and viable scenario. It assumes only two new fields: a scalar singlet and an inert scalar doublet, and is based only on renormalizable interactions, that slowly generate the dark matter asymmetry from the Standard Model Higgs asymmetry. The successful asymmetry transfer requires small (but technically natural) couplings which in turn make the model CP conserving in practice. The model allows for the direct detection of dark matter in the upcoming generation of experiments, and the inert doublet is predicted to be light enough to be potentially produced and observed at the LHC and future colliders, $46\,{\rm GeV}<580\,{\rm GeV}$.
