We demonstrate the use of these maps for identifying star-forming clumps, measuring radial star-formation profiles, detecting projected internal velocity gradients, deblending the H$\alpha$--[N II] complex, and assessing spectroscopic redshift measurements. As a first statistical application, we reconstruct the galaxy mass--metallicity relation for 885 galaxies observed with the blue grism at $0.4 < z < 0.9$ by deblending the H$\alpha$--[N II] complex in the emission-line maps, and measure stacked H$\alpha$ radial profiles for 2634 galaxies over the same redshift range. The mass--metallicity relation is consistent with that obtained from the Euclid 1D spectroscopic measurements, demonstrating overall agreement between the two deblending approaches. The recovered H$\alpha$ radial profiles broadly follow the $Y_{\mathrm{E}}$ stellar continuum but remain modestly more extended after matching the $Y_{\mathrm{E}}$ images to the H$\alpha$ PSF, consistent with previous results in the literature. Across the four $Y_{\mathrm{E}}$ size bins, we measure a mean $R_{50,\mathrm{H}\alpha}/R_{50,Y_{\mathrm{E}}}=1.15$.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.19308.title: Baryon Acoustic Oscillations from the all-sky Wen & Han cluster catalog and the 2MASS Redshift Survey
arxiv.org/abs/2611.19308.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.19308v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) in the clustering of galaxies and quasars now measure distances to precision of about one percent although galaxy clusters have so far given only marginal signals. We measure the BAO scale in the correlation function of \vNclus\ galaxy clusters with spectroscopic redshifts at $0.1<0.7$ from the Wen and Han (2024) all-sky catalog. After reconstruction of the density field, the BAO peak has a significance of $\vsigpost\sigma$ against a model without it, and gives $\DV/\rd=\vDVpost\pm\vDVpoststat\,({\rm stat})\pm\vDVpostsys\,({\rm sys})$ at an effective redshift $z_{\rm eff}=\vzeffv$, a \vfracposttot\% distance. We find that the statistical uncertainty is \vratiostat\ times smaller than that of the best earlier cluster measurement. The distance agrees with the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Data Release 2 within $\vnsdesipost\sigma$ and lies $\vnsplanckpost\sigma$ below Planck. We also measure the BAO scale in the \vTNgal\ galaxies of the 2MASS Redshift Survey with a mean effective redshift (weighted by $n\,w^2$ with FKP weights), $z_{\rm eff}=\vTzeff$ For this all-sky galaxy sample we obtain $\aiso=\vTpreA^{+\vTpreAup}_{-\vTpreAlo}$ before reconstruction.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.20300.title: Faster $\chi^2$ periodogram: Accelerating linear algebra with fast Toeplitz solvers
arxiv.org/abs/2611.20300.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.20300v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: In recent years, the traditional Lomb--Scargle periodogram, relying on least-squares fitting of a sinusoid to data with a known mean, has been mostly superseded by its floating-mean extension---the generalized Lomb--Scargle periodogram---due to the superior robustness and accuracy of the latter. While further generalization to higher-degree trigonometric polynomials (known as the multiharmonic analysis of variance and the fast $\chi^2$ periodogram) has been known for decades, its usage remains relatively uncommon, mostly due to its significantly higher computational cost. Here we present a technique reducing the computational complexity of such an extension by combining a Toeplitz formulation of the system of normal equations with non-uniform fast Fourier transforms, coupled with condition-number monitoring to protect against numerical instability. When modified for practical efficiency rather than asymptotic computational complexity, our approach reaches speed-ups exceeding an order of magnitude over current state-of-the-art implementations across a wide range of hyperparameters when evaluated on multithreaded systems, while matching or exceeding their accuracy. Additionally, we provide a reference implementation used for benchmarking, along with the code used to generate the results presented in this work.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.20884.title: Orbital decomposition and evolution of LEGA-C-like galaxies in IllustrisTNG from z = 1 to z = 0
arxiv.org/abs/2611.20884.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.20884v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Stellar orbits encode the dynamical history of galaxies and provide a physically motivated link between galaxy structures and assembly processes. Although orbit-based decompositions are well established in the Local Universe, their evolution across cosmic time, especially at higher redshifts, remains poorly explored. We investigate the orbital structure of \texttt{LEGA-C-like} galaxies in the \texttt{TNG100} simulation from $z=1$ to $z=0$ to identify how stellar mass, star formation activity, environment, merger history, gas content, and ex situ stellar mass growth shape their orbital transformation. We decomposed the stellar orbital structure of simulated galaxies into cold, warm, hot, and counter-rotating (CR) components using time-averaged orbital circularities. We find a strong mass dependence of orbital structure at $z=0$ as well as at $z=1$. Galaxies below $\log(M_\star/M_\odot)\sim11.2$ have a combined warm and cold orbital fraction of $\sim70\%$, whereas more massive systems have a hot-orbit fraction of $\sim60\%$. These trends are consistent with assembly pathways driven predominantly by wet and dry major mergers, respectively. Tracking the same galaxies to $z=0$ reveals a systematic, but mass-dependent, evolution toward lower rotational support: At both low and high stellar masses, the hot-orbit fraction increases, whereas the relative change is greater in low-mass galaxies. The survival of cold structure depends strongly on the star formation state at $z=1$; star-forming progenitors retain substantially larger cold fractions than the quiescent progenitors. At both redshifts, the orbital fractions show a rise (decline) in hot and CR (cold and warm) orbits with the ex situ stellar mass fraction at a fixed stellar mass. These results provide the first evolutionary framework for interpreting orbit-based decompositions of galaxies at the \texttt{LEGA-C} epoch.

arxiv.org/abs/2411.08097.title: Atomic Dark Matter, Interacting Dark Radiation, and the Hubble Tension
arxiv.org/abs/2411.08097.excerpt:
arXiv:2411.08097v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We present a new class of interacting dark sector models that can address the Hubble tension. Interacting dark radiation (DR) has previously been put forward as a solution to the problem, but this proposal is disfavored by the high-$\ell$ cosmic microwave background (CMB) data. We modify this basic framework by introducing a subcomponent of dark matter (DM) that interacts strongly with the DR, so that together they constitute a tightly coupled fluid at early times. We show that if this subcomponent decouples from the interacting DR during the CMB epoch, the $\ell$ modes of the CMB that entered the horizon before decoupling are impacted differently from those that entered after, allowing a solution to the problem. We present a model that realizes this framework, which we dub "New Atomic Dark Matter", or nuADaM, in which the interacting dark matter (iDM) subcomponent is composed of dark atoms, and dark "neutrinos" with long-range interactions contribute to the DR, hence the name of the model. This iDM subcomponent is acoustic at early times but decouples from the DR following dark recombination. In contrast to conventional atomic dark matter (ADM) models, the dark photon is part of a richer DR sector, which ensures that it continues to be self-interacting even after recombination. We show that this model admits a significantly larger value of $H_0$ than $\Lambda\mathrm{CDM}$ when fit to CMB and BAO data, while maintaining a comparable goodness of fit. Once the SHOES data set is included, it provides a significantly better fit than $\Lambda\mathrm{CDM}$.

arxiv.org/abs/2502.04374.title: The Numerics of VMEC++
arxiv.org/abs/2502.04374.excerpt:
arXiv:2502.04374v4 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: VMEC++ is a Python-friendly, from-scratch reimplementation in C++ of the Variational Moments Equilibrium Code (VMEC), a fixed- and free-boundary ideal-MHD equilibrium solver for stellarators and tokamaks. The first VMEC implementation was written by Steven P. Hirshman and colleagues in the 1980s and 1990s and its latest Fortran incarnation (PARVMEC, https://github.com/ORNL-Fusion/PARVMEC) is widely used in stellarator optimization systems. Our work improves on previous implementations with regard to various critical aspects: special care has been put in providing an idiomatic Python experience, from installation to actual usage; VMEC++ has a zero-crash policy; it supports inputs in the classic INDATA format as well as friendlier JSON files. VMEC++ execution times are typically less than or equal to previous implementations, and time to convergence can be decreased dramatically by leveraging its hot-restart feature: by providing the output of a VMEC++ run as initial state for a subsequent one, VMEC++ is initialized using the previously converged equilibrium. This can dramatically decrease runtimes when running on many similar magnetic configurations as it typically happens in stellarator optimization pipelines. On the flip side, some features of the original Fortran VMEC implementation are not yet available in VMEC++, such as support for non-stellarator-symmetric configurations. This contribution presents the internal numerics of the open-source VMEC++ package publicly for the first time.

arxiv.org/abs/2509.14701.title: Enhancement of Weak Interactions in Phase Transitions in Condensed Matter and Early Universe
arxiv.org/abs/2509.14701.excerpt:
arXiv:2509.14701v4 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Parity-violating weak interactions produce extremely small energy differences between left- and right-handed chiral systems. We show that these microscopic effects may be amplified during collective phenomena such as phase transitions. The enhancement factor is proportional to the critical number of atoms, $N_c$, in the nucleus of the new phase. Measurement of the ratio of produced left- and right-handed chiral structures may provide a way to determine $N_c$. Experiments in which spin-chiral structures are formed in ZnCr$_2$Se$_4$ during a phase transition in crossed electric and magnetic fields indicate an effective amplification corresponding to $N_c\sim 10^9-10^{10}$. We emphasize, however, that such large values cannot be inferred from homogeneous capillary nucleation alone, since the same parameters imply a very large nucleation barrier; in real crystals heterogeneous nucleation, defects, strain, and domain-growth dynamics may be essential. We also discuss, more cautiously, whether analogous collective enhancement could operate in first-order cosmological phase transitions beyond the Standard Model. The Standard-Model electroweak transition for the observed Higgs mass is a crossover and therefore has no critical bubble nucleus.

arxiv.org/abs/2604.06090.title: Posterior Predictive Checks for Gravitational-wave Populations: Limitations and Improvements
arxiv.org/abs/2604.06090.excerpt:
arXiv:2604.06090v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: When selecting a model to characterize an astrophysical population, it is crucial to assess whether that model fits the data and, if not, how it can be improved. To this end, posterior predictive checks (PPCs) are a widely-used statistical test of model fit when inferring gravitational-wave source populations. However, PPCs exhibit limitations when assessing single-event parameters with large measurement uncertainty, like the spin tilt angles of the binary black holes (BBHs) observable with the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) detectors. When single-event inference is prior-dominated, traditional PPCs fail to flag even very poor model fits. In this work, we assess the efficacy of various alternative PPCs on poorly-constrained parameters. We compare PPCs conducted on event- vs. data-level parameters (e.g. posterior samples vs. maximum likelihood points), and explore two additional event-level PPCs: partial predictive checks and split predictive checks. Independent of measurement uncertainty, we find that PPCs on maximum likelihood parameters are always more discerning of model misspecification than any event-level PPC. However, when investigating simulated GWTC-3.0-like catalogs, none of the alternative PPCs show significant improvement over those traditionally used, indicating that at that sensitivity, any limited information in the data about spin tilts is insufficient to diagnose model misspecification. Finally, we apply our suite of PPCs to the spin magnitude and tilt distributions inferred in the most recent LVK catalog, GWTC-4.0. We conclude that the Gaussian Component Spins model used therein under-predicts BBHs with large spin magnitudes and over-predicts those with perfectly anti-aligned tilts.

arxiv.org/abs/2604.21755.title: Quantum-information diagnostics of cosmological perturbations with nontrivial sound speed in inflation
arxiv.org/abs/2604.21755.excerpt:
arXiv:2604.21755v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: In this work, we systematically investigate the quantum-information diagnostics of cosmological perturbations with a nontrivial sound speed, utilizing a normalized open two-mode squeezed-state framework. Rather than introducing new observables, our analysis focuses on how a modified sound speed dynamically reshapes the Schr\"odinger evolution of the squeezing parameters ($r_k$ and $\phi_k$). We demonstrate how these dynamical changes are inherited by the reduced density matrix of the observable sector. By employing a sound-speed-resonance parametrization, we derive and evaluate the purity, von Neumann entropy, R\'enyi entropies, and logarithmic negativity. We introduce a bounded variable $x = \tanh r_k$ and perform numerical simulations within the inflationary regime. Our numerical results reveal that a nontrivial sound speed significantly suppresses the purity of the reduced state, indicating enhanced effective mixedness. Simultaneously, it strongly amplifies and modulates both the entropic and entanglement diagnostics. More precisely, a nontrivial sound speed postpones the onset of classicality by modulating the decoherence process. Ultimately, we show that a nontrivial sound speed leaves distinct and identifiable quantum-information signatures within the entanglement structure of the early universe.

arxiv.org/abs/2605.14572.title: Modifications of CMB Temperature and Polarization Quadrupole Signals in Thurston Spacetimes
arxiv.org/abs/2605.14572.excerpt:
arXiv:2605.14572v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Recent cosmological tests have discovered persistent CMB anomalies in the large-scale isotropy of the universe. Motivated thus by such anomalies that hint at potential departures from statistical isotropy present in recent cosmological observations with the advent of the 'precision cosmology' era, we are led to explore the viability of anisotropic Thurston geometries, described in William Thurston's geometrization conjecture. In this work, we examine the coherent temperature and polarization signals generated in the CMB sky by such geometries. We begin with introducing Thurston spacetimes as our background models and the formalism we use to obtain the patterns. We then construct a set of transfer equations relative to a given background and solve them for each spacetime geometry. We finally discuss the role of spatial curvature in these FLRW limiting models along with their underlying geometry, and attempt to establish some general results on the symmetries of the patterns produced by their time evolution in terms of temperature and Stokes parameters P, Q and U. We show the evolution of temperature and polarization amplitudes in terms of such Stokes parameters at different redshifts and attempt to isolate individual Thurston geometries.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.01236.title: Improving the resolution of double white dwarf systems with spaceborne gravitational wave observatories using a robust astrophysical prior
arxiv.org/abs/2606.01236.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.01236v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Resolving the crowded population of double white dwarf (DWD) binaries in data from spaceborne gravitational wave (GW) observatories (e.g., LISA, Taiji) remains a major analysis challenge. Comparable performance on addressing this problem has been achieved with two main approaches: global fit, in which resolvable sources are estimated simultaneously from the data, and iterative, where sources are estimated one at a time and subtracted out from the data. While the latter is computationally efficient, methods developed under this approach have traditionally followed a frequentist framework that ignores astrophysical priors. This work incorporates a strong astrophysical prior, derived from the mass limits of detached white dwarfs and linking the GW signal frequency $f$ with its time derivative $\dot{f}$, into the iterative \fitalgoname{} pipeline. Applied to simulated LISA and LISA-Taiji network data, the method increases the number of confidently resolved sources by ${\approx}7.3\%$ (LISA-only) and ${\approx}14.6\%$ (network) at matched detection rate, respectively, and improves parameter estimation accuracy.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.15680.title: Assessing the enrichment of heat-producing elements in deep-mantle structures using a directional geoneutrino detector
arxiv.org/abs/2606.15680.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.15680v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Determining the spatial distribution of heat-producing elements (HPEs) within the Earth is critical for understanding the planet's thermal and chemical evolution. A central debate is whether domains in the deep mantle, particularly the Large Low-Velocity Provinces (LLVP), represent anomalous, radiogenically enriched reservoirs. Variation in the surface flux of geoneutrinos provide a direct probe of Earth's internal radioactivity. However, current continental located detectors measure only the angle-integrated flux, leading to strong spatial trade-offs that substantially limit the ability of practical networks to uniquely resolve mantle compositional heterogeneity. In this study, we quantify the potential of directional geoneutrino detection to overcome this limitation. By evaluating realistic LLVP geometries in the context of the proposed Ocean Bottom Detector (OBD), we demonstrate that resolving the incoming direction of geoneutrinos can substantially improve the precision with which HPE enrichment in LLVPs can be constrained relative to the surrounding mantle, for a range of target angular resolutions envisioned for a future directional geoneutrino detector. These results indicate that future directional geoneutrino measurements could help determine whether LLVP host enhanced HPE abundances and assess their contribution to Earth's radiogenic heat budget. Such measurements would provide a new observational constraint on the chemical heterogeneity of the deep mantle and its role in Earth's long-term thermal evolution.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.20957.title: Out-of-Equilibrium Effects in Non-Radial Relativistic Stellar Perturbations: A Model-Agnostic Formulation and Mode Analysis
arxiv.org/abs/2606.20957.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.20957v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We present a systematic, model-agnostic analysis of out-of-equilibrium effects, including viscosity and thermal conductivity, in non-radial oscillations of relativistic stars. Extending the Lindblom-Detweiler formalism, we construct, to our knowledge, the first general framework for linear, non-radial relativistic stellar perturbations that incorporates generic nonequilibrium corrections to the perfect-fluid sector in both the even- and odd-parity channels. Our framework is formulated in terms of the tensorial structure and thermodynamic decomposition of generic corrections without relying on any specific constitutive relations, thereby allowing us to elucidate, at a structural level, how these effects enter the perturbation equations and contribute to geometric deformations and fluid fluctuations. As an application, we consider the Bemfica-Disconzi-Noronha-Kovtun fluid and perturbatively investigate shifts in the frequencies and damping times of modes connected to their perfect-fluid counterparts in the limit of vanishing transport coefficients. We also identify structural features of the closed eigenvalue problem that suggest the possibility of additional mode families. Our formalism provides a unified framework for analyzing how different relativistic fluid theories modify the structure of non-radial stellar perturbations.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.21925.title: From the Early Slope to Curvature: Future Prospects and challenges for Astrophysical Parameter Estimation Using the Core-Collapse Supernova High-Frequency Feature
arxiv.org/abs/2607.21925.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.21925v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Gravitational-wave (GW) signals from core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe) contain both stochastic and deterministic components. Among these, the High-Frequency Feature (HFF), associated with Proto-Neutron Star (PNS) oscillations, has emerged as an observable for probing dense-matter physics. Previous studies of the HFF have primarily focused on its early-time slope as a diagnostic of PNS contraction and its dependence on the nuclear equation of state (EOS). In this work, we investigate recovering higher-order features of the HFF evolution, such as its curvature, from core-collapse supernova numerical simulations. By analyzing 2D and 3D waveforms injected into real interferometric noise, we apply the coherent WaveBurst algorithm in its cWB-XP implementation to reconstruct the HFF of recovered events. Comparing reconstructions at different signal strengths allows us to examine the extent to which the HFF remains accessible beyond its early linear evolution

arxiv.org/abs/2609.10111.title: Multiparameter quantum bounds for entanglement-assisted aperture synthesis
arxiv.org/abs/2609.10111.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.10111v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Entanglement-assisted optical interferometry promises diffraction-limited imaging over baselines where light cannot be physically combined, but its estimation-theoretic bounds exist only for a single visibility on one baseline. This work formulates the multiparameter quantum estimation problem for an M-station array. A reduction lemma shows that the multimode quantum Fisher information (QFI) equals the mean photon number times the QFI of a single delocalized photon, making the problem finite-dimensional. The local photon-number superselection rule erases all phase information from the bare state; shared entanglement restores a fraction f(r)=r/(1+r) of the QFI on a baseline supplied with r pairs, a benchmark that applies to every pair of the array. The QFI matrix and its mean Uhlmann curvature show numerically that a point source is measurement-compatible, whereas every extended-source model examined is incompatible; a semidefinite-programming evaluation shows that the Holevo bound exceeds the symmetric-logarithmic-derivative bound by up to ~24% for three stations and by 4-8% for larger arrays and for CHARA. An explicit collective receiver, a numerically optimised global linear-optical network with photon counting, attains a weighted variance within 2-9% of the Holevo bound, over an order of magnitude below an explicit pairwise receiver, and a noisy-resource threshold gives the break-even baseline (~22 km for illustrative parameters) beyond which distributed entanglement beats direct transmission. Finally, allocating a finite entanglement budget has a closed-form proportional (square-root-law) solution for a per-baseline fringe cost, whereas for the source-parameter variance under an explicit photon budget the routing of photons matters far more than the entanglement split. These results recast quantum aperture synthesis as collective multiparameter estimation, illustrated on CHARA.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.12719.title: Stochastic gravitational waves from narrow-band cosmological magnetic fields
arxiv.org/abs/2610.12719.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.12719v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We calculate the spectrum of gravitational waves generated by a cosmological magnetic field with a narrow-band power spectrum. For a magnetic spectrum narrowly peaked at a comoving wavenumber $k_c$, we find that the gravitational wave signal has a maximum at $2k_c$ and, as expected from momentum conservation, has a sharp cutoff at that scale. We apply this analysis to an ultralight dark matter model of magnetogenesis operating around recombination, in which an axion-photon coupling generates a helical magnetic field by parametric resonance. We determine the conditions for the resulting gravitational waves to enter the frequency range of pulsar timing experiments. Although the required frequency can be reached for sufficiently large coupling, the corresponding amplitude is below the experimental sensitivity for physically allowed energy densities of the magnetic field. We generalize this conclusion to models of magnetogenesis operating at other epochs, estimating as $T \simeq 160$ MeV the temperature of a magnetogenesis process assumed to be the source of the stochastic gravitational wave background suggested by pulsar timing arrays. We place the lower bound $T \gtrsim 1$-10 MeV on such viable models.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.37198.title: Searches for new particle physics by methods of classical and neutrino astronomy
arxiv.org/abs/2610.37198.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.37198v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Selected astrophysical methods for testing particle-physics models are reviewed. Stellar structure and evolution constrain additional channels of energy loss and transport; high-energy photon propagation probes photon mixing with new particles and modifications of electron-positron pair production; large-volume neutrino telescopes are used to search for magnetic monopoles, neutrinos from superheavy dark-matter decay, and non-standard neutrino propagation. Recent applications of these methods are discussed, involving the tip of the red-giant branch in the color-luminosity diagram, gamma-ray burst 221009A, and data from the Baikal Gigaton Volume Detector (Baikal-GVD) and the IceCube experiment. In each case, particle-physics parameters are inferred through a forward model that accounts for the response to new physics, propagation, detection, and nuisance parameters.

phys.org/news/2026-11-broken-circuits-gr.excerpt: Inside electronic devices, electric current can gradually displace atoms within tiny metal connections, creating gaps or unwanted accumulations that eventually cause circuits to fail. This phenomenon, known as electromigration, has long been regarded as a reliability problem that engineers must work to prevent. Yet the ability of an electric current to move atoms also raises the possibility of putting that movement to constructive use, directing atoms through a material rather than allowing them to migrate uncontrollably.

phys.org/news/2026-11-microplastics-airb.title: Microplastics make up 1 in 100 airborne particles sampled at four Michigan schools
phys.org/news/2026-11-microplastics-airb.excerpt: One in 100 of the tiny particles hanging in the air we breathe in Michigan is a microplastic, according to a University of Michigan study. The study tested the air for microplastics in four locations across lower Michigan, all in the parking lots of K-12 schools. It found that microplastics constitute about 1% of particles found in the atmosphere.

phys.org/news/2026-11-phantom-forests-of.title: Phantom forests: How low-integrity offsets lead to policy failure
phys.org/news/2026-11-phantom-forests-of.excerpt: Australia's Safeguard Mechanism (SGM) is failing to reduce emissions and drive decarbonization in the industrial and mining sectors because of an overreliance on cheap, low-integrity offsets, according to a new report titled "Phantom Forests and the Safeguard Mechanism: How Low-integrity Offsets are Obstructing Climate Action."

phys.org/news/2026-11-dark-personality-t.title: Dark personality traits linked to better chance at getting a second date
phys.org/news/2026-11-dark-personality-t.excerpt: Some personalities stand out on the first date and end up being asked for a second date, but not the ones we expect. While very few people want to date people with dark traits like psychopathy and sadism, they seem to make a good first impression. Psychopathy involves traits such as manipulation, low empathy and impulsivity, while sadism involves taking pleasure in others' suffering. Yet, on a first date, these traits don't necessarily stop someone from coming across as an appealing romantic partner.

phys.org/news/2026-11-hostility-online-d.title: Hostility in online heat wave discussions shows signs of contagion, study suggests
phys.org/news/2026-11-hostility-online-d.excerpt: Anger and frustration can run high in online discussions about climate change. But a new study led by Nanyang Technological University, Singapore (NTU Singapore) suggests that hostility in these conversations tends to follow earlier hostility, hinting that people may pick up uncivil behavior from others.

phys.org/news/2026-11-fierce-tropical-do.title: Why fierce tropical downpours thrive in a relatively dry atmosphere
phys.org/news/2026-11-fierce-tropical-do.excerpt: Twenty years of weather radar observations around Darwin have helped researchers investigate a surprising feature of tropical rain: the fiercest local downpours tend to occur when the surrounding atmosphere is relatively dry.

phys.org/news/2026-11-successful-high-pu.title: Successful high-purity synthesis of the challenging-to-produce cerium orthoferrite!
phys.org/news/2026-11-successful-high-pu.excerpt: A research team including scientists from Ehime University successfully synthesized high-purity CeFeO3, a difficult-to-produce cerium–iron mixed oxide, using hydrogen reduction. By optimizing hydrogen concentration and gas flow rate, they achieved a phase purity of up to 99 mol%. The team also clarified the formation mechanism and identified factors that hinder synthesis. This method, published in the journal Inorganic Chemistry, provides a foundation for future research into applications in magnetic materials and catalysis.

phys.org/news/2026-11-eyes.html.title: Trying to hide some information? Your eyes might give you away
phys.org/news/2026-11-eyes.html.excerpt: Many people believe there are obvious ways to spot a liar without listening to a word they say, such as shifty glances and nervous fidgeting. Psychologists, however, are increasingly looking past these supposed telltale signs, which aren't necessarily reliable, toward subtler, involuntary clues that can be harder to detect.

phys.org/news/2026-11-key-eu-committee-w.title: Key EU committee backs EU-wide restrictions on 'forever chemicals'
phys.org/news/2026-11-key-eu-committee-w.excerpt: The European Chemicals Agency said Thursday that one of its expert committees was backing EU-wide restrictions on so-called "forever chemicals," citing risks to both the environment and health.

phys.org/news/2026-11-nasa-voyager-home-.title: NASA's Voyager 1 phones home from an awe-inspiring 1 light-day away
phys.org/news/2026-11-nasa-voyager-home-.excerpt: NASA's Voyager 1 has phoned home from one light-day away, humanity's first emissary to cross this monumental threshold way out in interstellar space.

phys.org/news/2026-11-astronomers-remark.title: Astronomers discover remarkable triple-star system just 28 light-years from Earth
phys.org/news/2026-11-astronomers-remark.excerpt: Astronomers have discovered a stellar system just 28 light-years from Earth that challenges our understanding of how stars live, die and interact as they evolve.

phys.org/news/2026-11-factors-exacerbate.title: Study identifies factors that exacerbated the 2024 flash flood in l'Horta Sud
phys.org/news/2026-11-factors-exacerbate.excerpt: The severity of the flooding experienced by l'Horta Sud on Oct. 29, 2024, can be explained by a combination of exceptional rainfall, near-simultaneous rises in several ravines and a heavily urbanized area, according to a study carried out by the Institute of Water and Environmental Engineering at the Universitat Politècnica de València (UPV), which reconstructs the event using rainfall data and mathematical models capable of simulating how rain is transformed into runoff, how water carries sediment and how the flood spreads across the territory.

phys.org/news/2026-11-dna-strands-chaoti.title: Long DNA strands turn chaotic fluid motion into a steady rhythm
phys.org/news/2026-11-dna-strands-chaoti.excerpt: In living cells, tiny molecules can generate coordinated motion across distances thousands of times larger than the molecules themselves. How such small movements give rise to coordinated motion over much larger distances is still not fully understood.

phys.org/news/2026-11-blue-decrease-phyt.title: A blue desert: Researchers record decrease in phytoplankton in Monterey Bay due to El Niño
phys.org/news/2026-11-blue-decrease-phyt.excerpt: MBARI's advanced technologies continuously monitor the oceanographic and biological conditions in Monterey Bay. These instruments and the decades of data they have collected are invaluable as MBARI scientists work to understand how the historic 2026–2027 El Niño will affect marine life and ecosystems.

phys.org/news/2026-11-unexpected-effect-.title: Unexpected spin effect lets electric currents switch antiferromagnets at room temperature
phys.org/news/2026-11-unexpected-effect-.excerpt: Researchers have discovered a physical effect that expands the fundamental understanding of how electric currents interact with magnetism, revealing an unexpected way to manipulate the magnetic state of antiferromagnetic materials. A research team led by Northwestern Engineering's Pedram Khalili has discovered what it calls octupole-driven spin-transfer torque (OTT). The effect allows an electrical current to manipulate the magnetic state of a class of materials called noncollinear antiferromagnets.

phys.org/news/2026-11-fridges-packaging-.title: Fridges and packaging contribute to food waste
phys.org/news/2026-11-fridges-packaging-.excerpt: Food waste depends not only on what people do but also on how refrigerators and packaging are designed. This is the conclusion of a study from Linköping University (LiU) in Sweden. Information campaigns are not enough. Refrigerators and packaging must also be designed based on how people actually behave, according to the researchers.

phys.org/news/2026-11-brazil-approach-de.title: Brazil's approach to deforestation delivers major reductions in Amazon forest loss
phys.org/news/2026-11-brazil-approach-de.excerpt: A new study finds that a Brazilian policy aimed at reducing deforestation appears to be remarkably effective and has significantly reduced forest loss in the Brazilian Amazon. The largest reductions occurred on private lands specifically targeted by Brazil's Priority List (PL) policy, with no evidence that deforestation shifted to other land ownerships or neighboring municipalities.

A new study by Yale School of the Environment scientists that focuses on Chicago found that it is widespread across the city, yet much of it sits in neighborhoods where current zoning doesn't allow that housing type.

phys.org/news/2026-11-ai-optimize-sensor.title: Researchers use AI to optimize sensor design for ultrasensitive vitamin C detection
phys.org/news/2026-11-ai-optimize-sensor.excerpt: Researchers led by Professor Jinsung Park from the Department of Biomechatronic Engineering at Sungkyunkwan University (SKKU), have developed an ultrasensitive electrochemical sensor capable of detecting extremely low concentrations of vitamin C. By incorporating artificial intelligence (AI) into the sensor development process, the research team identified promising fabrication conditions using a limited amount of experimental data, reducing the need for extensive trial-and-error optimization.

sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261118.title: Scientists tested 212 plant-based foods. Every single one contained fungal toxins
sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261118.excerpt: A new study has uncovered a surprising concern hiding in popular plant-based foods and drinks. Researchers tested 212 vegan and vegetarian products sold in the UK, including meat alternatives, oat milk, almond milk, and soy milk, and found that every single one contained at least one potentially harmful fungal toxin. Known as mycotoxins, these naturally occurring compounds can contaminate grains, legumes, and seeds during farming and storage.

sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261118.title: This 6-million-year-old whale may have had the most crooked face in mammal history
sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261118.excerpt: A bizarre whale that lived roughly 6 million years ago had a face so dramatically crooked that scientists believe it may have been the most asymmetrical of any mammal. Discovered in Peru, the extinct pygmy sperm whale Scaphokogia huachafo had an enormous downward-curving snout and a skull so distorted that researchers initially thought it had been damaged after death. Instead, its strange anatomy appears to have been an extraordinary evolutionary adaptation for hunting along the seafloor.

sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261118.title: Is free will an illusion? New brain research reveals a surprising twist
sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261118.excerpt: New research reveals that the brain makes free choices and forced decisions using surprisingly similar neural processes, with activity building toward a decision before we act. The discovery challenges assumptions about free will while suggesting that our personal preferences and experiences still shape what we choose.

sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261118.title: Something strange is living beneath the skin of deep-sea pigs
sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261118.excerpt: Scientists have discovered a strange bacterium hiding beneath the skin of deep-sea creatures known as sea pigs, revealing an unexpected biological partnership. The microbe has an unusually tiny genome, yet more than a quarter of its DNA is devoted to making surface proteins, some of them exceptionally large. Researchers suspect it depends heavily on its host for survival, but what the sea pigs gain in return remains a mystery.

sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261118.title: Why hydrogen flames can glow orange, then turn nearly invisible
sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261118.excerpt: Hydrogen flames can shift from bright orange to nearly invisible depending on something unexpected: tiny amounts of sodium floating in the air. Scientists say this discovery could help make future hydrogen-powered stoves and ovens safer by replacing visual flame detection with specialized sensors.

sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261117.title: This strange creature lived 309 million years ago, long before the dinosaurs
sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261117.excerpt: More than 300 million years ago, long before dinosaurs roamed Earth, the Chicago area was a steamy, swampy landscape teeming with bizarre creatures. Now, scientists at the Field Museum have identified a previously unrecognized species of ancient amphibian ancestor, revealing new clues about the evolution of frogs and salamanders.

sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261117.title: Too much exercise could leave your brain stuck in overdrive
sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261117.excerpt: Exercising too much without adequate recovery may disrupt brain chemistry in surprising ways. Scientists found that mice subjected to prolonged, intense training had elevated dopamine levels in a brain region linked to memory and emotions, even 48 hours after exercising. The discovery could help explain why overtrained athletes sometimes struggle with insomnia, anxiety, and persistent fatigue, although these symptoms were not directly measured.

The Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) was by pretty much all measures a resounding success when it struck the asteroid moonlet Dimorphos going more than 22,000 kilometers per hour. In these "strange metals," electrical resistance rises in a straight line with temperature over a very wide range. Electrons seem to lose their momentum at the fastest rate quantum mechanics allows, the so-called Planckian limit. What causes this is still an open question.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.24949.title: Direct inference of cosmological mass growth via timing of black hole - pulsar binaries
arxiv.org/abs/2611.24949.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.24949v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Cosmologically coupled black holes (CCBHs) respond to the expansion of the Universe, independently of conventional astrophysical processes. Recent CCBH solutions in General Relativity demonstrate evolution of gravitating mass $m_{\rm BH}\propto a^\kappa$, where $a$ is the cosmological scale factor. This can be tested through the orbital period timing of black hole (BH) pulsar (PSR) binaries. In contrast to previous methods used to constrain $\kappa$, pulsar timing measurement baselines span decades instead of gigayears, allowing sources of bias to be well-controlled. As a test case, we analyze the globular cluster BH+PSR candidate J0514--4002E (spin $P\sim 5.6~{\rm ms}$, orbital period $P_{\rm b}\sim 7~\rm days$) under the assumption that the companion is a CCBH. Taking the difference between the observed orbital and spin period derivatives removes all kinematic effects, leaving only the pulsar's intrinsic spin-down $\dot{P}_{\rm int}$ as unknown. Setting $\dot{P}_{\rm int} = 0$, its physical minimum, gives a robust upper bound $\kappa \leqslant 3.95$ at $95\%$ confidence. We estimate $\dot{P}_{\rm int}$ through the population of millisecond pulsars matched in spin and infer $\kappa = 0.82 \pm 1.67$ and $0.75 \pm 1.54$, using $H_0 = 67.6$ and $73.5\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, respectively. Adopting typical baseline scaling of timing precision, the value $\kappa = 3$, argued elsewhere to link energized vacuum BH interiors to accelerated cosmological expansion, can be excluded or detected for this $2.35^{+0.20}_{-0.18}\,M_\odot$ companion at $3\sigma$ and $5\sigma$ confidence by 2031 and 2036, respectively.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.24976.title: Improving On-board Shape Models Using Sun Sensors and Implicit Representations
arxiv.org/abs/2611.24976.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.24976v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose an original, end-to-end approach to generate and refine the onboard 3D shape model of irregular small bodies, such as asteroids, using only low-cost Sun sensor eclipse data and coarse a priori knowledge, tailored for resource-constrained missions like CubeSats. Leveraging EclipseNets, a differentiable neural model of eclipse boundaries, our pipeline first refines 2D silhouettes by learning from real-time entry and exit events during spacecraft orbits, avoiding the limitations of traditional imaging or lidar in bandwidth-starved environments. These silhouettes then supervise a compact neural signed-distance field with periodic activations, enabling incremental updates to a high-fidelity implicit geometry representation capable of capturing fine-scale features and concavities. In simulations of the body Eros under realistic orbital dynamics, the method increases silhouette IoU from 0.70 to 0.87 and produces coherent 3D reconstructions, suggesting our approach could find a place in future autonomous architectures for small-body exploration.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.24991.title: Testing the Universality of RAR Model with Constraints on Fermionic Dark Matter for M31
arxiv.org/abs/2611.24991.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.24991v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The Ruffini--Arg\"uelles--Rueda (RAR) model describes dark matter as a self-gravitating system of massive fermions in thermodynamic equilibrium within general relativity. It suggests a dual morphology in galaxies: a highly degenerate quantum core mimicking a central supermassive black hole, and a classical halo that explains galactic rotation curves. Earlier applications of the model to the Milky Way restricted the fermion mass to $mc^{2}=48\text{--}345~\text{keV}$, and the orbits of the S-stars around Sagittarius~A$^{\ast}$ (Sgr~A$^{\ast}$) favored $mc^{2}=56~\text{keV}$, whereas a recent thermodynamic stability analysis allows only $mc^{2}\approx194\text{--}387~\text{keV}$. In this work, we apply the RAR model to the Andromeda galaxy (M31), which hosts a dark compact object of approximately $1.4\times10^{8}~M_{\odot}$ within $0.19~\text{pc}$, roughly 33 times the mass of Sgr~A$^{\ast}$. We solve the relativistic equilibrium equations for $mc^{2}=6\text{--}60~\text{keV}$. For all these masses, the fermionic core lies within $0.19~\text{pc}$ and provides the central mass without a black hole. With a bulge and disk added, the total rotation curve is statistically acceptable ($\chi^{2}/N_{\text{dof}}\approx1.18$) but lies below the disk data at $3\text{--}11~\text{kpc}$, an offset attributed to the baryonic models we adopted. The Navarro--Frenk--White (NFW) and Burkert profiles fitted to the same data give a lower $\chi^{2}$ but require an additional black hole. The stability of the M31 core against gravitational collapse limits the fermion mass to $mc^{2}\lesssim60~\text{keV}$. With the earlier Milky Way range, a single fermion can therefore describe both galaxies only for $mc^{2}=48\text{--}60~\text{keV}$, which includes $56~\text{keV}$. With the thermodynamic range, no fermionic core can supply the central mass of M31, so M31 would have to host a black hole.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.25023.title: Eos: a merger-induced starburst at the dawn of Galactic low-$\alpha$ disc formation
arxiv.org/abs/2611.25023.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.25023v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The last significant merger of the Milky Way, the Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus (GS/E), is thought to have reshaped the early Galaxy and to mark the transition from the high-$\alpha$ to the low-$\alpha$ disc. The stars formed in situ during this merger offer a direct record of that epoch but are hard to identify. Using APOGEE DR17 abundances, we study Eos, a population of in-situ low-$\alpha$ stars on halo-like, non-rotating, eccentric orbits. The metal-poor part of Eos has a nitrogen dispersion as large as that of the pre-disc Aurora population and up to 1.7 times that of the low-$\alpha$ disc at the same metallicity. Heating alone cannot produce this: the Splash, a disc heated onto halo orbits by the same merger and selected in the same way, shows no excess over its parent disc. This part of Eos was therefore born in poorly mixed gas. Eos is also chemically intermediate between the accreted GS/E debris and the coeval in-situ Milky Way stars, and stars with more GS/E-like chemistry move on more extended orbits. Its stars are older than the bulk of the low-$\alpha$ disc but younger than the high-$\alpha$ disc and the Splash. We compare these observations with a merger-induced starburst seen in an Auriga simulation. There, a GS/E-like merger funnels the stripped progenitor gas into a mixing lane of intermediate metallicity, where stars form with intermediate abundances, a large chemical dispersion and a chemodynamical gradient set by their birth site, reproducing the observed signatures of Eos. We therefore interpret Eos as the surviving relic of the GS/E merger-induced starburst, born largely from the partially mixed gas bridging the two galaxies and marking the onset of the Milky Way's low-$\alpha$ disc. Eos thus provides a direct observational view of the star formation and galaxy evolution driven by the Milky Way's last significant merger.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.25024.title: The OGLE Collection of Variable Stars. Over 1.3 Million Human-Verified Eclipsing and Ellipsoidal Binaries in the Milky Way
arxiv.org/abs/2611.25024.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.25024v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present a new release of the OGLE collection of eclipsing and ellipsoidal binary systems in the Galactic bulge and disk. The catalog contains 1 330 024 objects, including 1 280 765 eclipsing binaries and 49 259 ellipsoidal variables, nearly three times as many systems as the previous editions of the OGLE collection. The selection and classification process involved expert visual inspection of the light curves. The catalog incorporates all available OGLE-II, OGLE-III, and OGLE-IV photometry, extending the observational baseline to nearly 28 years for some objects. The orbital periods and other observational parameters of previously known systems have been updated. We present basic statistics of the sample and highlight selected rare and unusual systems.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.25027.title: Top-heavy Initial Mass Functions are not enough at cosmic dawn
arxiv.org/abs/2611.25027.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.25027v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A top-heavy stellar initial mass function (IMF) has been proposed to explain the unexpected abundance of ultraviolet (UV)-bright galaxies at cosmic dawn. We test this possibility using the metallicity-dependent, top-heavy IMF recently proposed by Chon et al. (2024), which is motivated by simulations of metal-poor star formation. We compare this IMF with a Salpeter IMF, self-consistently including the associated changes in UV emission, supernova feedback, metal enrichment, and dust production. At fixed star formation rate, the Chon IMF enhances the intrinsic UV luminosity by a factor ${B}_{1500}\simeq4.7$-$2.8$ over halo masses $M_h=10^{8-12}\,M_\odot$. However, its larger supernova rate suppresses star formation and increases dust attenuation, reducing the net boost to ${B}_{\rm UV}\simeq2.0$-$1.06$. For halos relevant to the bright end of the UV luminosity function, the enhancement is only ${B}_{\rm UV}\simeq1.2$-$1.4$, or about $0.3$ mag. Calculations with the DELPHI semi-analytic model confirm that the self-consistent Chon and Salpeter UV luminosity functions differ by less than $0.5$ dex at $z\simeq11$-$17$. Thus, a top-heavy IMF alone cannot explain the bright galaxy excess. Conversely, the predicted pair-instability supernova abundance differs by factors of $2$-$6$ between the two IMFs, providing a potentially cleaner observational diagnostic of the high-mass stellar populations at these early epochs.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.25035.title: Influence of variable IMF on the dynamical black hole mass estimates in massive ETGs
arxiv.org/abs/2611.25035.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.25035v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Several studies have shown that the stellar initial mass function (IMF) in massive early-type galaxies (ETGs) is not universal. Recent results from stellar population synthesis models, based on integral-field unit (IFU) observations, indicate that the IMF varies radially, becoming increasingly bottom-heavy towards galaxy centres. This radial variation alters the stellar mass-to-light ratio ($\rm M_{*}/L$) and can significantly affect dynamical black hole (BH) mass estimates in massive ETGs. In this study, we investigate the impact of a radially varying IMF on BH mass estimates for five massive galaxies: NGC3923, NGC4261, NGC4636, IC4296, and IC4329. Using DYNAMITE, a triaxial Schwarzschild orbit-based modelling code, we perform mass modelling of these galaxies based on MUSE and SINFONI IFU observations. Our models incorporate radially varying stellar $\rm M_{*}/L$ profiles derived from spatially resolved stellar population modelling with a free IMF, and we compare the resulting BH masses with those obtained from dynamical models assuming a constant stellar $\rm M_{*}/L$. All galaxies in our sample show bottom-heavy IMFs in their central regions, with the IMF generally becoming lighter towards larger radii. We obtain constrained BH masses for NGC3923 and IC4329, while only upper limits are obtained for NGC4261, NGC4636, and IC4296. Compared with the constant-$\rm M_{*}/L$ models, the variable-$\rm M_{*}/L$ models yield BH masses lower by approximately 83% and 11% for NGC3923 and IC4329, respectively, while the BH mass upper limits for the other galaxies can increase or decrease. Our results demonstrate that spatial variations in the IMF and stellar $\rm M_{*}/L$ can have a non-negligible but strongly galaxy-dependent impact on dynamical BH mass measurements. These results highlight the importance of accounting for such variations in future dynamical modelling efforts.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.25036.title: Simulation-based inference for gravitational-wave cosmology: parameter reconstruction of a first-order electroweak phase transition
arxiv.org/abs/2611.25036.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.25036v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) from a cosmological first- order phase transition would be unambiguous evidence for physics beyond the Standard Model, with a strong electroweak phase transition (EWPT) at LISA as a prime example. Reconstructing the underlying model from such a signal is challenging, since the map from the model parameters to the spectrum is degenerate and strong transitions occupy only small and sparse regions of parameter space. We show that simulation-based inference (SBI), a likelihood-free approach applicable to generic SGWB sources, provides a reliable parameter reconstruction despite these difficulties. We first apply SBI to the thermodynamic parameters characterizing the transition, namely its strength, inverse duration, temperature and bubble wall velocity. As a concrete application, we then consider a strong EWPT in a singlet extension of the Standard Model and reconstruct the model parameters from the resulting SGWB. We find that the SBI posteriors agree with those of a likelihood-based Markov chain Monte Carlo analysis, at negligible cost per data set once the network has been trained. Using the network posterior as the proposal for importance sampling with the exact likelihood further corrects its remaining deviations, at a sampling efficiency several orders of magnitude higher than sampling from the prior. SBI thus offers a fast and flexible framework for the cosmological science case of LISA

arxiv.org/abs/2611.25039.title: Twisted resonant orbits: Quantifying the deceleration of the Galactic bar
arxiv.org/abs/2611.25039.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.25039v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent structural discoveries in Gaia Data Release 3 reveal distinct, chevron-shaped over-densities in the radial phase space of the halo. Although initial interpretations identify these features as the phase-mixed relics of a past galaxy merger, their prominent asymmetry and persistence at high metallicities strongly challenge this interpretation. These features are better explained as a dynamical response to a Galactic bar, where stars are trapped in resonances. We establish the fractional $v_r$ asymmetry of the chevrons as a quantitative diagnostic tool for the bar's rotational state. We utilise test-particle simulations of a Milky Way-like galaxy to model various bar pattern speed evolutions, including decelerating and constant speed scenarios. By mapping the fractional asymmetry of the phase-space chevrons across a parameter space of bar deceleration rates and pattern speeds, we establish a direct correlation between the bar's deceleration and the rotational response of the resonant orbits. Comparing these simulated constraints with observational data from Gaia DR3 provides a framework for measuring the current deceleration of the Galactic bar, and a probe of the amount of dynamical friction occurring between the baryonic and dark matter content of the Milky Way. We find a dimensionless deceleration parameter $\eta \equiv - \dot{\Omega}_b/\Omega_b^2 = 0.0015^{+0.0016}_{-0.0009}$, equivalent to $\dot{\Omega}_b = -2.23^{+1.50}_{-2.46} \, \text{km s}^{-1} \text{kpc}^{-1} \text{Gyr}^{-1}$, in agreement with previous estimates obtained with independent methods. Gaia DR4 should sharpen this measurement considerably.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.25049.title: Ram Pressure Is Unable to Strip All Phases of the Interstellar Medium out of Spirals Falling into Galaxy Clusters
arxiv.org/abs/2611.25049.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.25049v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Following the expansion of the Universe, spiral galaxies may fall at large speeds into galaxy clusters. Their interaction with the intracluster medium (ICM) may remove part of their gas and reduce their capacity for making new stars, as envisaged by Gunn & Gott. Ram pressure stripping (RPS) is commonly invoked to explain this gas loss and the wakes or tails left behind in-falling galaxies. Here we revise the impact of RPS on individual dense clouds and particularly focus on turbulent viscous stripping (TVS), driven by Kelvin-Helmholtz instabilities at the cloud-ICM interface, that affects the high-density and low-temperature molecular gas. For an extended gaseous body to decelerate, momentum from its exposed surface must be communicated into the gas by a hydrodynamic disturbance able to propagate through it. Three-dimensional hydrodynamic calculations follow this interaction with dense clouds. At cloud number densities $n_{\mathrm{cl}}=10^2$ cm$^{-3}$, ram pressure acting through the transmitted shock strongly compresses and deforms the cloud and produces only a small deceleration; at $n_{\mathrm{cl}}=10^3$ cm$^{-3}$, the slower transmitted shock produces much weaker deformation. At both cloud densities, TVS continuously removes gas from the cloud surface and forms qualitatively indistinguishable trailing wakes, with comparable mass-loss rates, suggesting that TVS acting on individual dense clouds can generate filamentary substructure within jellyfish-galaxy tails.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.25079.title: Validation and Physical Characterization of Seven TESS Exoplanets: A Compact Multi-Planet System and Targets for Atmospheric Spectroscopy
arxiv.org/abs/2611.25079.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.25079v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) continues to identify thousands of transit candidates that require statistical validation to rule out astrophysical false positives before atmospheric characterization can be pursued. We statistically validate and characterize seven TESS exoplanet candidates orbiting five host stars. As a consistency check of our automated vetting and Bayesian inference pipeline, we include TOI-2392.03, a sub-Neptune companion previously validated in the literature. Our framework combines automated signal retrieval, pixel-level centroid and Gaia DR3 contamination analysis, and false positive probability (FPP) computation with the TRICERATOPS vetting engine. Physical and orbital parameters are derived via nested sampling (juliet/Dynesty), complemented by an empirical mass-radius relation, since no dynamical mass measurements are available. Applying the same procedure to all candidates, we statistically validate six new exoplanets ($\mathrm{FPP} < 0.015$ and $\mathrm{NFPP} < 0.001$), one of which (TOI-7721.01) lies close to the FPP threshold. We report the period ratios of the three-planet system TOI-2392, and identify TOI-7721.01 and TOI-1277.02 as the candidates with the highest Transmission Spectroscopy Metrics (TSM) in our sample, making them targets of interest for atmospheric follow-up with the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and the upcoming Ariel mission.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.25080.title: EuclidFM: Foundation Model for Compact Photometric Survey Representation
arxiv.org/abs/2611.25080.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.25080v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present EuclidFM, a compact self-supervised model that learns object-level representations from heterogeneous catalogue photometry in Euclid Quick Data Release 1. Using 90,258 sources across three Euclid Deep Fields, a masked-autoencoder Transformer reconstructs withheld fluxes and uncertainties from available measurements, producing a 128-dimensional embedding per source. The embeddings encode morphological and photometric information: sources with high point-like probability have, on average, 12.4 similarly classified neighbours among their 15 nearest neighbours, compared with 4.3 under field- and magnitude-stratified randomization. Linear models trained on frozen embeddings predict VIS magnitudes with correlations of 0.954-0.980 across three held-out fields. For sources with VIS aperture-flux uncertainties up to 1 microJy, incorporating embeddings reduces the root-mean-square error in predicted log uncertainty by at least 24% relative to a magnitude-only model. A classifier trained on spectroscopically confirmed sources identifies 1,150 quasar candidates, but only 21 of the 156 candidates with accepted external counterparts show AGN evidence, including 12 spectroscopic quasars. The classifier's transferability to the wider photometric catalogue therefore remains uncertain, and its purity and completeness require further evaluation. Independently of classification, EuclidFM provides a common representation for downstream survey analyses when photometric coverage differs between sources. Code and data are available at https://github.com/AI-Driven-HEP/EuclidFM.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.25084.title: Kinetic Tomography with Diffuse Interstellar Bands in APOGEE DR17
arxiv.org/abs/2611.25084.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.25084v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Context: Mapping gas flows in the interstellar medium is key to understanding the formation of structure in our Milky Way. Methods that simultaneously reconstruct clouds' distances and line-of-sight velocities are called kinetic tomography (KT). Diffuse interstellar bands (DIBs) are powerful tracers for such maps because they trace the integrated dust density and the dust-weighted velocity. Previous DIB-KT works had small samples with coarse kpc-scale resolution and could not capture vertical disk structure. Aims: Make 4D (3D position + radial velocity) maps of the Milky Way from new, high-quality 15,273 {\AA} DIB detections in APOGEE DR17. Methods: We combine variational inference and Gaussian processes with a mixture likelihood for low signal-to-noise detections and marginalization over distance uncertainties. We calibrate the model on mock fields and spectral injection tests and validate the map against independent tracers of the dust density (3D dust maps) and velocity substructure (masers and young stellar clusters). Results: We recover a posterior distribution over 3D maps of the density and velocity structure of the 15,273 {\AA} DIB within 6 kpc of the Sun. We measure the large-scale structure of the DIB disk (scale length, height and flare) and detect vertical distortions consistent with the warp. On smaller scales, the map resolves distance ambiguities in gas longitude-velocity diagrams. From the second-order velocity structure function, we measure a slope (0.64 $\pm$ 0.04) consistent with Kolmogorov turbulence, amplitude consistent with expectations for molecular clouds, and a preliminary ratio of compressive-to-solenoidal modes. Conclusions: With larger DIB catalogs expected from SDSS-V, this framework should resolve kinematic substructure at the scales needed to constrain the formation and dynamics of individual clouds and voids. (abridged)

arxiv.org/abs/2611.25085.title: Off-Nuclear AGN Signatures in MaNGA: Spatially resolved selection using MEGACUBES
arxiv.org/abs/2611.25085.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.25085v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present a spatially resolved search for off-nuclear active galactic nucleus (AGN) candidates in the MaNGA survey. Using megacubes, we analyze over 10,000 galaxies, separating AGN activity from diffuse ionized gas with refined equivalent-width and surface-brightness thresholds. Combining a spatial radial algorithm with BPT, WHaN, and WHaD diagnostics, we classify 261 nuclear AGNs, 201 off-nuclear AGNs, and 159 'quiet' (composite-spaxel-dominated) sources. We test whether off-nuclear AGNs reside in distinct host galaxies or whether the offset is a local, gas-driven phenomenon. Nuclear and off-nuclear AGN hosts are statistically indistinguishable in stellar mass, age, star formation rate, and gas-phase metallicity. However, the excitation and kinematics of the AGN-ionized gas differ significantly: nuclear AGN spaxels have [O III]$\lambda5007$ luminosities $\sim 0.7$ dex higher than off-nuclear spaxels, whose lower [O III]/H$\beta$ ratios indicate genuinely lower-excitation gas rather than an obscured view of the central engine. We also find an orientation trend: 72% of nuclear hosts are face-on, versus 50% of off-nuclear hosts, so projection effects contribute to, but do not fully explain, off-nuclear detections. The classical WHaN boundary at $\log$([N II]/H$\alpha$) = -0.4 misclassifies high-metallicity diffuse ionized gas in integral field data; an empirical shift to -0.25 removes over 48,000 spurious AGN spaxels. Finally, the off-nuclear fraction implies an episodic AGN phase lifetime of $\sim 5 \times 10^4$ yr, consistent within a factor of a few with independent fading-AGN estimates and supporting short, recurrent accretion bursts.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.25092.title: Spiral Pitch Angles in Black Hole Images and Movies
arxiv.org/abs/2611.25092.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.25092v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) has produced images of M87* and Sgr A*, and will soon produce time sequences of images, or movies. General relativistic magnetohydrodynamics (GRMHD) models predict EHT sources will exhibit brightness fluctuations along the ring. The fluctuations are commonly connected to trailing spiral features. Here, we introduce a method to measure the pitch angle $\psi$ of radially extended features by cross-correlating brightness fluctuations sampled on rings at two distinct impact parameters. Pitch angle can be reliably measured from synthetic movies with BHEX resolution, and can be constrained even at EHT resolution. Single images enable noisy constraints of $\psi$. Pitch angle depends most on the viewing inclination and black hole spin. For constant inclination, the spiral winding direction depends on the sign of spin, with spirals winding more tightly in the direction of frame dragging near the horizon. The pitch angle will complement other observables to reliably constrain both the source inclination and spin in future analysis by EHT, and by expansions to the EHT such as ngEHT and BHEX.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.25093.title: Revealing galaxy assembly bias with luminosity-weighted marked correlations
arxiv.org/abs/2611.25093.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.25093v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We investigate whether luminosity-weighted marked correlation functions can reveal secondary halo information beyond that encoded by halo mass alone, as expected in scenarios of galaxy assembly bias. We propose a controlled null test in which galaxy luminosities follow the same mean luminosity--halo mass relation and scatter, while their residuals are either (A) uncorrelated with secondary halo properties or (B) correlated with a standardized secondary halo property, $s$. Both models have identical halo occupation, galaxy positions, luminosity function, and unweighted projected two-point correlation function, $w_p(r_p)$, so their distinction is encoded entirely in the luminosity marks. At leading order, the projected marked correlation function difference, $\Delta\mathcal{M}_p(r_p)$, scales as $\rho^2\sigma_{\log L}^2\xi_{ss}(r_p)$, where $\rho$ controls the coupling between the luminosity and secondary-property residuals, $\sigma_{\log L}$ is the scatter in log luminosity at fixed halo mass, and $\xi_{ss}$ describes the spatial correlation of the secondary property. We test this framework using a DESI-BGS mock catalogue over $0.1<0.4$. For the injected dependence, we detect a marked-clustering deviation over $0.11<1.04$, obtaining $\chi^2=30.14$ relative to the null covariance. A one-parameter test rejects the mass-only hypothesis at greater than $5\sigma$ significance ($p=2.13\times10^{-7}$) for $|\rho|>0.63$. At fixed $\sigma_{\log L}=0.23$, correlations as weak as $|\rho|\simeq0.52$ remain detectable, with the results stable under variations in the HOD prescription and modelled galaxy selection effects. These results establish luminosity-weighted marked clustering as a sensitive null test for property-based galaxy assembly bias and secondary halo information hidden from unweighted two-point clustering.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.25110.title: A novel pathway to stellar-mass black hole growth: Re-accretion of gas from stellar wind bubbles
arxiv.org/abs/2611.25110.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.25110v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The formation of high-mass stellar black holes (BHs) observed in mergers by gravitational wave observatories remains difficult to explain using standard models of stellar evolution. We investigate whether newly formed stellar-mass BHs in dense molecular clouds can significantly increase their final mass by accreting gas from pre-existing, wind-blown interstellar bubbles produced by their progenitor stars. We performed 1D and 3D hydrodynamic simulations of interstellar bubbles driven by stellar feedback, incorporating thermal conduction, radiative cooling, gravity, ionizing radiation, stellar winds, and supernova (SN) explosions. We modeled the subsequent accretion onto the central BH for two formation scenarios: core-collapse SN and direct collapse. Our parameter space study encompasses over 500 1D simulations, varying initial cloud densities, gravitational binding energies, progenitor masses ($40-257\,M_\odot$), and metallicities ($0.66\,Z_\odot$ and $0.016\,Z_\odot$), and tracks the bubble evolution for millions of years post-BH formation. Scenarios exhibiting significant re-accretion were further validated using high-resolution 3D simulations. Our simulations show that BHs formed via direct collapse from low-metallicity progenitors can accrete up to $6.9\,M_\odot$ of gas from massive inner shells formed by late-stage slow winds, resulting in final BH masses of up to $93\,M_\odot$. Conversely, we find no significant re-accretion in scenarios involving an SN explosion or high-metallicity progenitors; in these cases, fast winds or SN ejecta efficiently evacuate dense structures from the bubble interior, leaving behind a hot, low-density medium. [abridged] This mechanism may help explain the unexpectedly high masses of BHs observed in gravitational wave events.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.25120.title: On the High Eccentricity Orbit of 51 Eri b and Constraints on Interactions with a Second Companion
arxiv.org/abs/2611.25120.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.25120v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The eccentricity of an exoplanet's orbit is a key observational quantity that can be used to infer its dynamical past and predict its future orbital evolution. Planets are expected to emerge from their protoplanetary cradles with roughly circular eccentricities, and non-circular eccentricites to arise from subsequent dynamical processing in the absence of the gas disk. We present an updated orbit for 51 Eridani b based on 5 years of 0.2 mas precision optical interferometry from VLTI/GRAVITY(+). This planet is young (${\sim}20\,\mathrm{Myr}$ old), temperate ($T_{\rm eff}\sim650\,\mathrm{K}$), and on a wide orbit ($a{=}9.36\,\mathrm{au}$) with an uncertain mass ($M_{\rm b}\leq12\,M_{\rm J}$). We measured the planet's motion to an exceptionally high precision, confirming that its orbit is very eccentric ($e_b=0.574\pm0.003$). We observe residuals to the absolute astrometry of the host star based on a single planet orbit that could be attributable to reflex motion from a third body in the system. We construct a two companion orbit model that could explain the apparent reflex motion of 51 Eri A: this model predicts that the putative second companion has $M_c\in[1.0, 2900]_{95\%}\,M_{\rm Jup}$ and $a_c\in[0.3, 3.1]_{95\%}\,\mathrm{au}$. In this framework, a dynamical interaction between b and ``c" could have kicked the exterior, lower mass b out onto its present, eccentric orbit. If this signal is astrophysical, and not due to a systematic error, this candidate should be confirmable with Gaia DR4 epoch astrometry in the near future.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.25125.title: Intra-day variability of the gamma-ray/optical emission of 3C 454.3: the complexity beyond the long-term correlation
arxiv.org/abs/2611.25125.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.25125v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Simultaneous $\gamma$-ray/optical observations probe particle acceleration and radiative processes in blazar jets. The blazar 3C 454.3 shows a significant long-term correlation between these bands, often interpreted as support for the canonical one-zone leptonic emission model. However, both bands show strong intra-day variability, and whether the correlation persists during individual flares remains unclear.
  We study the $\gamma$-ray/optical correlation and intra-day variability of 3C 454.3 over 17 years (2007--2024), on timescales $\leq 24$ h.
  We analyse AGILE and Fermi-LAT observations using light curves binned from 3 to 48 h, together with simultaneous $R$-band photometry from WEBT and public optical data sets. We examine the flux and spectral evolution of individual flares, estimate time-dependent correlation properties, and derive Compton dominance from optical and $\gamma$-ray luminosities.
  We confirm the long-term correlation, but find large intrinsic dispersion and a slope of $\eta \simeq 1.6$--$1.7$, inconsistent with a single canonical one-zone scenario. On shorter timescales, correlation strengths range from weak to strong, with slopes spanning $\eta \simeq 0.4$--$2.0$. We also find orphan flares in both bands, diverse flare morphologies, distinct Compton-dominance patterns with rapid excursions from $\sim 10$ to 120, and heterogeneous spectral trends. The shortest resolved variability timescales ($t_{\rm var} \lesssim 3$ h) indicate that localized emission regions are required by causality.
  The $\gamma$-ray/optical correlation in 3C 454.3 thus arises not from a single emission regime, but from multiple epoch-dependent physical states. Increasing temporal resolution reveals richer variability, highlighting the importance of systematic intra-day, multi-epoch studies of bright FSRQs.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.25203.title: Where Did the Angular Momentum Go? WASP-12 b May Have Circularized on a Retrograde Orbit
arxiv.org/abs/2611.25203.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.25203v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: WASP-12 b is the only exoplanet with confirmed orbital decay. Angular momentum transferred from its decaying orbit should have realigned the star's thin convective layer, yet an earlier Rossiter--McLaughlin (RM) measurement suggested a $\sim$60$^\circ$ spin--orbit misalignment. We present two new Keck Planet Finder RM measurements. We measure a sky-projected obliquity of $\lambda=-1.3\pm8.7^\circ$; and the star's projected rotation velocity is $v\sin i_\star=1.3\pm0.1~\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, an order of magnitude lower than expected for a star of its mass and age. With WASP-12's low chromospheric activity, $\log R^\prime_{\rm HK}=-5.5$, our analysis favors an aligned system in which $v\sin i_\star$ reflects slow surface rotation with $P_{\rm rot}\sim60$ days, rather than a projection effect. Our evolution models favor a late-main-sequence star rather than a subgiant, with a central convective core found in 99\% of posterior samples. This internal structure suppresses the central-focusing and nonlinear wave-breaking mechanisms for inward-propagating gravity waves. We propose that WASP-12 b was initially placed on a retrograde orbit after high-eccentricity migration, when its host rotated at $v\sin i_\star\approx14$~km~s$^{-1}$ (or $P_{\rm rot}\sim$6 days). Tidal decay transferred orbital angular momentum to the convective envelope, aligning the surface. The retrograde interior acts as an angular-momentum reservoir, while interior--envelope coupling slows the surface rotation. A semi-empirical relation gives an envelope--interior angular-momentum exchange timescale of $\sim4$~Myr, similar to the observed orbital-decay timescale of $\sim3.25$~Myr. The angular-momentum budget also permits this initially retrograde evolution. In contrast, an initially prograde planet would have spun up the surface rotation to a rate substantially higher than observed.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.25217.title: Rediscussion of eclipsing binaries. Paper 33. The A-type system CW Canis Majoris in the PLATO southern field
arxiv.org/abs/2611.25217.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.25217v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: CW CMa is a detached eclipsing binary containing two A0 V stars in a circular orbit of period 2.12 d. We analyse the light-curves of this system from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) together with published radial velocity measurements to determine the masses and radii of the component stars to high precision, obtaining masses of 2.087 +/- 0.022 Msun and 1.972 +/- 0.024 Msun, and radii of 1.841 +/- 0.012 Rsun and 1.748 +/- 0.014 Rsun. We detect a changing orbital period over the four available TESS sectors indicative of the presence of a companion on a wider orbit. We develop a new method to determine the effective temperatures of the component stars using their measured radii, the Gaia parallax, and surface-brightness calibrations to reduce the degeneracy between temperature and extinction. The method gives temperatures of 9850 +/- 280 K and 9570 +/- 270 K and an interstellar extinction of A(V) = 0.32 +/- 0.06 mag. The properties of the system can be matched by theoretical models for a subsolar metal abundance (Z = 0.010) and an age of 400 +/- 20 Myr. CW CMa has been selected as a target for the PLATO satellite, with which it will be observed for at least two years.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.25220.title: Multiphase Gas in High-$z$ Cosmic Sheets
arxiv.org/abs/2611.25220.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.25220v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present high-resolution cosmological simulations of individual cosmic sheets ($z=3-6$) using the moving-mesh code AREPO to study cold gas ($T\approx10^4\rm ~K$) in the diffuse cosmic web. We find cosmic sheet gas forms a fragmented morphology, evident as kiloparsec-scale variations in the neutral hydrogen column density ($N_{\rm HI}$). Fragmentation arises from the bending and disruption of the cold-dense sheet core into a multiphase medium. Nonlinear thin shell instability (NTSI) and later shear-induced vorticity drive this bending, rather than previously suggested thermal or Richtmyer-Meshkov instabilities. Higher resolution enhances fragmentation. Across a fourfold range in spatial resolution, $N_{\rm HI}$ covering fractions increase by factors of $\approx 1.5-3.5$ for partial Lyman-limit systems (pLLS) and Lyman-limit systems (LLS). An order-of-magnitude estimate suggests sheets may host a large fraction of the ultra-low metallicity (p)LLS population. Equivalent MP-Gadget simulations show qualitatively similar fragmentation, but numerical smoothing effects are present. Cosmic-sheet gas properties remain unconverged despite our high resolutions.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.25221.title: The HI Mass Fractions of Milky Way Analog Samples
arxiv.org/abs/2611.25221.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.25221v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We estimate average HI mass fractions, f_HI = M_HI/M_star, for nine Milky Way analog samples (MWAs): galaxies selected on similarity to the MW in terms of various properties. We find most (seven) MWAs have lower  than a recent estimate for the MW, although only the two largest have significantly lower estimates.
