We suggest that either the MW has an unusual f_HI for its properties, or we are overestimating its HI content, one of many challenging global measurements to make from our perspective inside our own Galaxy.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.25230.title: The SPACE Program IV: Atmospheric Features on the Cold Transiting Sub-Neptune TOI-6478 b
arxiv.org/abs/2611.25230.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.25230v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Among the current population of exoplanets there are very few sub-Neptunes that have their atmospheric composition identified. This is primarily due to sub-Neptunes having high metallicity, clouds, and/or hazes obscuring absorption features. This often produces a spectrum that presents itself as a featureless spectrum especially in the near-IR. However, there are tentative trends that suggest sub-Neptunes with the lowest equilibrium temperatures ($\mathrm{T_{eq} < 400\:K}$) have detectable features, perhaps due to inefficient haze production or cloud sedimentation. TOI-6478 b is a low-density sub-Neptune exoplanet ($\rm <\mathrm{9.9\:M_{\oplus}}$ and $\rm \sim 4.5R_{\oplus}$) with an equilibrium temperature $\mathrm{T_{eq} = 220 \:K}$ assuming zero albedo. In this study, we present the highest S/N spectral feature ($\sim$6) of any sub-Neptune detected using HST/WFC3. We detect this spectral feature using a robust analysis that incorporates the Transit Light Source Effect (TLSE) to rule out false detections due to stellar activity. With the narrow bandpass of HST we were unable to distinguish whether the spectral feature at 1.4$\mu$m is from H$_2$O or CH$_4$ absorption. Meanwhile, self-consistent atmospheric models provide physical motivation for CH$_4$ to be the dominant absorber given that H$_2$O should condense or cold trap at higher pressures. Through our analysis we determine that HST/WFC3 alone cannot distinguish between major absorbers. However, a broader wavelength coverage by JWST will be able to measure the atmospheric composition in detail, due to the high S/N features for this target.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.25255.title: Transition Zone from ExoEarth to ExoVenus: Critical Insight from Planets on the Edge
arxiv.org/abs/2611.25255.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.25255v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Venus and Earth, planets with similar masses and radii, provide astonishingly different environments, raising the question of why these two rocky worlds evolved so differently. Explaining this divergence is a central challenge in comparative planetology and astrobiology. Now, atmospheric studies of exoplanets can explore the possibilities of terrestrial planet evolution, especially in the era of JWST; however, we have not yet realized the critical insights rocky exoplanets in the Transition Zone (TZ) can provide. These TZ planets in the overlap between the Habitable Zone and Venus Zone can test how incident stellar irradiation affects surface water retention and habitability. Observations of exoplanets in the TZ can probe not only the emergence and decline of exoplanet habitability but also test hypotheses about Venus' past, complementing upcoming Venus flagship missions. Here, we analyze NASA's Exoplanet Archive, updated with Gaia DR3 data, and provide a target list of 23 rocky exoplanets in the Earth-to-Venus Transition Zone, along with 2 planets in the Venus Evolution Zone (EV). We examine their demographics and quantify their potential for follow-up observations. This list of rocky TZ and EV planets allows observers to optimize target selection and observing strategy for specific instruments. Characterizing exoplanets in the Transition Zone will be critical to investigating open questions about the emergence and decline of habitability on rocky worlds, the evolution from an exo-Earth to an exo-Venus, and Earth's future.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.25306.title: Sherlock 'Chrones: The Curious Case of NGC 6791 and Asteroseismic Targets Therein Reveals Mixing Length Dependence on Evolutionary Stage
arxiv.org/abs/2611.25306.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.25306v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As single-aged populations containing stars spanning a range of masses but otherwise with similar properties, star clusters provide valuable testbeds for stellar evolution theory. The old, metal-rich, open cluster NGC 6791 is well studied, but the availability of asteroseismic observations of individual cluster members allows for a more in-depth analysis. Driven by mounting evidence that the solar assumption for convection used in almost all 1D stellar models is not adequate, and in light of the increased precision provided by modern data and asteroseismic constraints, we built and compared custom isochrones with varying values of the convective mixing length, $\alpha_\text{MLT}$, to two clusters with well-determined ages: NGC 6791 and the well-studied, metal-poor globular cluster M92. For both clusters, we found that the best-fitting mixing length parameter decreases monotonically as a function of evolutionary phase, finding values between $0.98-1.10\alpha_{\odot}$ for NGC 6791 and $1.16-1.21\alpha_{\odot}$ for M92. In NGC 6791, this corresponds to an 18% decrease in the best fitting mixing length between the main sequence turn-off and upper end of the red giant branch. The degree of variation found within this one object is therefore comparable to variation across the literature in $\alpha_\text{MLT}$ fits for other non-solar targets, calling single-valued $\alpha_\text{MLT}$ fits to clusters into question. It is also consistent with $\log g$-$\alpha_\text{MLT}$ trends predicted by higher-fidelity, 3D convection analyses. Our results therefore illustrate the need for more flexibility in our treatment of the mixing length in isochrones to properly model clusters.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.24965.title: Exact ultrastatic multi-throat wormholes: Geometry, energy conditions, and optical cavities
arxiv.org/abs/2611.24965.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.24965v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We construct an exactly solvable hierarchy of static, spherically symmetric, wormholes with arbitrary finite throat multiplicity. A factorized prescription for the derivative of the areal radius places every stationary sphere at a prescribed proper distance while retaining elementary integrability and asymptotic flatness. The order-$N$ geometry contains exactly $N+1$ throats and $N$ anti-throats, arranged as an alternating chain of necks and finite interior cavities. Independently of this particular hierarchy, the Einstein equations imply three universal ultrastatic results. Every nondegenerate throat violates the radial null energy condition, whereas every nondegenerate anti-throat satisfies the null, weak, dominant, and strong energy conditions, with the strong-energy sum condition saturated. The same local combination $\rho+p_\ell$ fixes the radial stability of the associated circular null orbit through $V_{\mathrm {null}}''=8\pi L^2(\rho+p_\ell)/\mathcal R^2$; throats are therefore unstable light rings and anti-throats are stable ones. Finally, every finite cell between consecutive stationary spheres, each exterior cell, and the complete two-ended radial null geodesic carry strictly negative integrated radial null energy. The resulting spacetimes are exact multi-cavity optical chains whose cavity centers are locally nonexotic even though no cell can eliminate averaged radial exoticity. The first nontrivial member interpolates continuously from the Ellis-Bronnikov wormhole through a quartically degenerate throat to a double-throat geometry and admits closed expressions for its source, null average, branchwise Morris-Thorne form, embedding criterion, and traversability scales. Its vanishing Arnowitt-Deser-Misner mass follows from the specific radial falloff of the hierarchy, rather than from ultrastaticity alone.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.25029.title: Dirac leptogenesis with charged leptons
arxiv.org/abs/2611.25029.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.25029v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Popular frameworks that explain the baryon asymmetry of the Universe (BAU) are electroweak baryogenesis, requiring a first-order phase transition, and Majorana leptogenesis, which relies on lepton number violation in the neutrino sector. Dirac leptogenesis offers an alternative mechanism that avoids both requirements, instead allowing the BAU to follow from previously generated chiral asymmetries that remain out of equilibrium in the early Universe. Conventional realizations of this scenario typically invoke ultra-light Dirac neutrinos. In this work, we generalize the mechanism to include Standard Model charged leptons by assuming that their mass-generating interactions have a UV origin and arise from higher-dimensional operators. For concreteness, the analysis is performed within a Froggatt-Nielsen setup, which allows us to naturally address fermionic mass hierarchies, too, now linked to the BAU, and we show that the proposed mechanism is viable by supercooling the flavon phase transition. The framework predicts a flavon with a (1.7-50) GeV mass, bounded by the non-observation of lepton flavor violation and the requirement for the Universe to not reheat above sphaleron temperatures, which could be indirectly probed by future lepton flavor violation experiments.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.25040.title: Subsolar neutron star-black hole binaries from collapsars: Gravitational waveform models and detectability in current searches
arxiv.org/abs/2611.25040.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.25040v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Detecting subsolar objects in binary mergers would be an exceptional discovery in gravitational wave astronomy. So far, dedicated searches for subsolar coalescences reported no confident detections, setting upper bounds on their merger rate. Given that standard stellar evolution is not able to produce subsolar candidates, a confident detection would point either to new physics or to unconventional astrophysical pathways. These include collapsars, where the outer parts of neutrino-cooled accretion disks around newborn stellar-mass black holes are subject to fragmentation and give rise to subsolar neutron stars, which can later merge with the central black hole. We show that current subsolar searches may miss a significant fraction of these neutron star-black hole mergers, because their templates do not account for the small mass ratios, the tidal disruption of the neutron star, and the effects of the surrounding gas. This result motivates improving the waveform modeling used in current subsolar searches and building adequate template banks tailored to these systems.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.25156.title: A universal modal-noise limit for multimode photonic systems
arxiv.org/abs/2611.25156.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.25156v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Modal noise limits the photometric and spectroscopic stability of every multimode-to-single-mode photonic system, yet it is quantified device by device. For isotropic modal excitation at fixed input power, the fractional power fluctuation of any linear multimode system is shown to be fixed by one number: the participation ratio M_eff of the eigenvalues of K = T{\dag}WT. Monte Carlo for spatially filtered fibres, lossy lanterns, and integrated mode converters confirms the law, which recovers the classical speckle limits. Extending K to K({\lambda}) gives the spectral correlation of modal noise and a closed-form velocity error, maximal when the correlation width equals the line width.

arxiv.org/abs/2506.01786.title: Science Prospects for the Southern Wide-field Gamma-ray Observatory: SWGO
arxiv.org/abs/2506.01786.excerpt:
arXiv:2506.01786v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Ground-based gamma-ray astronomy is now well established as a key observational approach to address critical topics at the frontiers of astroparticle physics and high-energy astrophysics. Whilst the field of TeV astronomy was once dominated by arrays of atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes, ground-level particle detection has now been demonstrated to be an equally viable and strongly complementary approach. Ground-level particle detection provides continuous monitoring of the overhead sky, critical for the mapping of extended structures and capturing transient phenomena. As demonstrated by HAWC and LHAASO, the technique provides the best available sensitivity above a few tens of TeV, and for the first time access to the PeV energy range. Despite the success of this approach, there is so far no major ground-level particle-based observatory with access to the Southern sky. HESS, located in Namibia, is the only major gamma-ray instrument in the Southern Hemisphere, and has shown the extraordinary richness of the inner galaxy in the TeV band, but is limited in terms of field of view and energy reach.
  SWGO is an international effort to construct the first wide-field instrument in the south with deep sensitivity from 100s of GeV into the PeV domain. The project is now close to the end of its development phase and planning for construction of the array in Chile has begun. Here we describe the baseline design, expected sensitivity and resolution, and describe in detail the main scientific topics that will be addressed by this new facility and its initial phase SWGO-A. We show that SWGO will have a transformational impact on a wide range of topics from cosmic-ray acceleration and transport to the nature of dark matter. SWGO represents a key piece of infrastructure for multi-messenger astronomy in the next decade, with strong scientific synergies with the nearby CTA Observatory.

arxiv.org/abs/2510.00124.title: What's in Your Transit? A Path to More Science from Exoplanet Transit Data
arxiv.org/abs/2510.00124.excerpt:
arXiv:2510.00124v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Transit-depth measurements can remain less precise than expected from photon noise alone, because limb darkening and orbital parameters are inferred simultaneously with transit depth. We refer to this shortfall as the ``transit-depth precision problem'' and quantify it with an amplification factor, $A$, comparing the measured transit-depth uncertainty with baseline scatter. Using central-transit injection--retrieval tests informed by $\gt500{,}000$ MPS-ATLAS intensity profiles, we determine how limb-darkening prescriptions and priors affect both transit-depth precision and accuracy. We find that limb-darkening coefficients are the dominant contributors to the excess uncertainty, followed by inclination and stellar density, through parameter correlations. In the configurations tested, the widely used quadratic law can produce low $A$ yet substantially biased transit depths and wavelength-dependent structure in otherwise flat transmission spectra. Third-order polynomial and fourth-order nonlinear laws provide a better precision-accuracy tradeoff, although all quantitative results remain conditional on the adopted stellar models and transit geometry. Improved stellar models can increase observing efficiency by enabling tighter, accurate limb-darkening coefficient priors: in our fourth-order nonlinear tests, $10\%$--$20\%$ priors reduce transit-depth uncertainties by factors of $1.1$--$1.8$ relative to uniform priors, while stronger $1\%$ priors reduce them by $2.1$--$2.5$. Assuming uncertainty decreases as the inverse square root of the number of observed transits, these gains correspond to reaching the same target transit-depth precision with approximately $1$--$3$ and $4$--$6$ times fewer transits, respectively. We recommend testing multiple limb-darkening prescriptions and reporting wavelength-resolved sensitivity to limb-darkening assumptions.

arxiv.org/abs/2510.06786.title: A Giant Peanut-shaped Ultra-High-Energy Gamma-Ray Emitter Off the Galactic Plane
arxiv.org/abs/2510.06786.excerpt:
arXiv:2510.06786v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Ultra-high-energy (UHE) gamma($\gamma$) rays serve as unique probes for investigating new non-thermal astronomical phenomena within the Galaxy and also for studying PeV particle acceleration and propagation. Based on the UHE $\gamma$-ray survey conducted by LHAASO, this paper reports the discovery of a new source distinct from all previously identified high energy $\gamma$-ray objects. This source exhibits an elongated, peanut-like structure, which can be described as a rectangular strip measuring 4.6$^\circ$ in length and 0.45$^\circ$ in width, featuring two bright knots. It is located at a Galactic latitude of $-$17.5$^\circ$, well below the Galactic plane and away from regions rich in UHE sources. The energy spectrum is spatially uniform across the entire region and is well fitted by a power-law model with an index of $-$1.95 and a cutoff at 250 TeV. The highest detected photon energy reaches 760 TeV. Morphological and spectral analyses indicate the presence of a powerful particle accelerator in this region, capable of accelerating particles beyond 1 PeV. An energetic millisecond pulsar (MSP) J0218+4232 is located at the brighter end of this source, with a spatial chance coincidence probability of 3.6*10$^{-4}$, corresponding to 3.4$\sigma$. This suggests that the emission from this region very likely originates from particles accelerated within the MSP wind nebulae, potentially providing the first observational evidence supporting the wind nebulae of MSP as sources of UHE $\gamma$ rays. However, the presence of other hidden accelerators, whether associated with known or entirely new populations of PeVatrons, cannot be ruled out, motivating future multi-wavelength observations.

arxiv.org/abs/2602.12272.title: The Wandering Supermassive Black Hole Powering the off-nuclear TDE AT2024tvd
arxiv.org/abs/2602.12272.excerpt:
arXiv:2602.12272v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present an analysis of the spectral energy distribution (SED) of the off-nuclear tidal disruption event (TDE) AT2024tvd during its late-time plateau phase, combining X-ray spectra and UV/optical photometry. Using a fully relativistic, compact accretion disk model with self-consistent inner-disk Comptonization, we reproduce the observed SED without significant residuals. The inferred black hole mass ${\rm log}_{10}(M_{\bullet}/M_\odot) \approx 6.0 \pm 0.2$, and the inferred disk parameters place AT2024tvd within known TDE-disk scaling relations ($L_{\rm bol}^{\rm disk}/L_{\rm Edd} \propto T_{\rm p}^4 \propto M_{\bullet}^{-1}$, $L_{\rm plat} \propto M_{\bullet}^{2/3}$, $R_{\rm out}/r_{\rm g} \propto M_{\bullet}^{-2/3}$). Our results show that: (i) there is no currently detected star cluster or dwarf galaxy associated with the source, down to a mass limit of $\log_{10}(M_{\rm gal}/M_{\odot}) \leq 7.6$; (ii) the black hole is a wandering supermassive, rather than intermediate-mass, black hole; and (iii) the source represents an extreme case of black hole-to-host mass ratio, with $M_{\bullet}/M_{\rm gal} > 3\%$, consistent with a heavily tidally stripped nucleus. The latter aligns with cosmological simulations predicting that surviving host remnants of most wandering black holes should not retain a detectable stellar overdensity when located at small halo-centric distances. We discuss differences with previous analyses of this source and highlight why our modeling approach provides a more physically consistent solution with more reliable parameter inference.

arxiv.org/abs/2602.12970.title: Demographics of Off-Nuclear Tidal Disruption Events Powered by Wandering Black Holes
arxiv.org/abs/2602.12970.excerpt:
arXiv:2602.12970v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The four recently discovered off-nuclear tidal disruption events (TDEs)---EP240222a, AT2024tvd, AT2025abcr, and AT2023mfm---together with those found serendipitously over past decades (ESO 243-49 HLX-1 and 3XMM J2150-05), reveal a small but robust population of accreting off-nuclear, or ``wandering'' black holes (WBHs). We analyze their demographic properties in comparison to other populations, we find that (i) every event occurs in a massive early-type galaxy within the narrow range $10.7 \lesssim \log_{10}(M_\star/M_\odot) \lesssim 11.1$, a range that very rarely hosts nuclear TDEs; (ii) their radial displacements span $1 \lesssim R_{\bullet}/{\rm kpc} \lesssim 40$, or $0.003 \lesssim R_{\bullet}/R_{200} \lesssim 0.1$; (iii) a stellar counterpart is detected in pre-TDE observations only when located outside the galaxy's half-light radius; (iv) while nuclear TDE hosts are usually isolated, off-nuclear TDEs and quiescent WBHs are more likely to inhabit galaxy groups or clusters. Using the \texttt{ROMULUS} cosmological simulation, we show that all of these follow naturally from hierarchical galaxy formation. We construct the volumetric density of WBHs, $\phi_{\rm WBH}(M_{\star})$, which places the central 68\% of local WBHs in galaxies with $10.7 \lesssim \log_{10}(M_\star/M_\odot) \lesssim 11.3$, explaining (i) and (iv). This WBH distribution can imply a higher off-nuclear than nuclear TDE rate, at these galaxy masses. Their intrinsic radial distribution is Gaussian-like in $\log_{10}(R_\bullet/R_{200})$, consistent with (ii) except for a deficit of sources at the largest separations. Combined with parent-galaxy light, which suppresses counterpart detections at small separations, this distribution also explains (iii). These results show that off-nuclear TDEs are the accreting counterparts of the WBHs long predicted by cosmological simulations, and that they trace large-scale structure.

arxiv.org/abs/2603.03014.title: Reproducing the stellar-mass dependence of the giant planet occurrence rate with pebble accretion models
arxiv.org/abs/2603.03014.excerpt:
arXiv:2603.03014v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The stellar mass dependence of the unbiased giant planet occurrence rate may be the best statistical tool to constrain the formation of such planets. This rate rises and falls as a function of stellar mass, peaking around stars of $\sim 1.7{-}2 \Ms$. In this work, we carry out a population synthesis study, using pebble-driven core accretion model of planet formation, to investigate the planet formation conditions that may be responsible for this stellar-mass dependence. We use the inferred giant planet occurrence rated of three combined homogenised radial velocity surveys (EXPRESS, PPPS, and Lick giant star survey) to constrain the models. We find that we can produce a synthetic giant planet population with closely aligned occurrence and properties when we base our model on observationally-supported assumptions that accretion rates are higher and disk lifetimes are shorter around more massive stars, we can produce a synthetic giant planet population with closely aligned properties to the observed distribution. We also find that in this scenario, the runaway gas accretion occurs at a larger orbital distance and earlier times as the stellar mass increases.

arxiv.org/abs/2604.06308.title: Anisotropic hybrid stars: Interplay of superconductivity and magnetic field leading to gravitational waves
arxiv.org/abs/2604.06308.excerpt:
arXiv:2604.06308v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Neutron stars, at their cores, are highly dense and, thus, are expected to have a number of exotic processes. This includes a possible phase transition to deconfined quark matter at the core, leading to a hybrid star. The quark matter is expected to additionally be color superconducting. The physics of superconductivity plays an important role in understanding the high density matter in the interiors of neutron/hybrid stars. At their high densities, additionally, both proton superconductivity and neutron superfluidity are expected. We study the effect of superconducting (quark/proton) matter, along with the internal magnetic field, leading to pressure anisotropy within hybrid stars. We aim to probe the effect of superconductivity, especially from color superconducting quarks, on hybrid star structure. We propose new phenomenological model anisotropy profiles within a one-dimensional framework. We model quark matter using the vector interaction enhanced Bag model, and hadron matter with the DD2 equation of state. A Maxwell construction joins both phases. We further investigate the possible observational signatures of these hybrid stars. These include mass enhancement and the possibility of continuous gravitational waves arising from the anisotropy induced deformation, giving us a way to further constrain our model and its physical parameters.

arxiv.org/abs/2604.15430.title: GRMHD accretion beyond the black hole paradigm: Light from within the shadow
arxiv.org/abs/2604.15430.excerpt:
arXiv:2604.15430v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present the first three-dimensional general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulation of sustained accretion onto a horizonless singularity in which matter reaches the central object rather than being accumulated outside of it or expelled in outflows. We consider a Joshi-Malafarina-Narayan (JMN-1) spacetime, a well-motivated black hole mimicker that arises from gravitational collapse with anisotropic pressure in general relativity, and adopt a compactness parameter for which the central singularity is null. We find that the system evolves into a sustained magnetically arrested disk state. For parameters appropriate to the low-luminosity active galactic nucleus M87*, we obtain an accretion rate of $\sim(3.0 \pm 0.5)\times 10^{-6} \dot{M}_{\rm Edd}$, in full agreement with estimates based on black hole models and, in particular, comparable to that of our reference Schwarzschild black hole simulation. Synthetic ray-traced images at $230\,{\rm GHz}$, computed using polarized general relativistic radiative transfer, are broadly consistent with the Event Horizon Telescope observations of M87*. We identify a key observational discriminant between a black hole and JMN-1: the presence of detectable brightness inside of the ``observable" shadow of JMN-1. This emission originates very close to the central singularity, in a region that would be hidden behind the event horizon in a black hole spacetime. Although this signature is beyond the reach of current observations, it falls within the projected imaging dynamic range of next-generation radio interferometric instruments, offering a robust test of the black hole paradigm.

arxiv.org/abs/2604.28012.title: Rapid polarization position angle variations in FRB 20240114A point to a magnetospheric origin
arxiv.org/abs/2604.28012.excerpt:
arXiv:2604.28012v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs), thought to originate from magnetars, exhibit diverse polarization properties that constrain their emission physics and local magneto-ionic environments. The polarization position angle (PPA) is particularly sensitive to magnetic-field geometry in the emitting region and propagation effects in the magnetosphere and beyond. In hyper-active repeaters, PPAs are typically stable within bursts and over timescales of hours to days.
  Here, we present observations of the repeating source FRB~20240114A, which show significant burst-to-burst PPA variations. Using full-Stokes, high-time-resolution observations from the Nan\c{c}ay Radio Telescope (1.1--1.8\,GHz) and the Effelsberg 100-m telescope (1.3--1.5\,GHz) over $\sim1$~year, we measure rotation measures (RMs), polarization fractions, and time-resolved PPAs across 12 epochs.
  The RMs remain stable, and the emission is predominantly highly linearly polarized, with $\sim81\%$ of bursts showing $L/I > 0.8$, while circular polarization is weaker ($\sim16\%$ with $|V/I| > 0.1$). We find no evidence for Faraday conversion.
  The PPA exhibits rapid, stochastic variations from milliseconds to hours, spanning $\pm90^\circ$ during two active periods and $\pm50^\circ$ in a third. The distribution of PPA jumps shows that (1) there is no difference in the distribution of jumps on timescales shorter or longer than 1\,s; (2) positive and negative jumps are equally likely; and (3) a jump of $\pm90^\circ$, as expected from, e.g., orthogonal mode jumps, is not more common than any other value.
  This combination of stable RM, high linear polarization, and extreme PPA variability is not seen in other hyper-active repeaters. These results disfavor emission from a single fixed region and instead suggest multiple emission regions and/or strong magnetospheric and foreground propagation effects, such as plasma lensing.

arxiv.org/abs/2605.10354.title: STEPSIC: Initial condition generator for stereographic cosmological simulations
arxiv.org/abs/2605.10354.excerpt:
arXiv:2605.10354v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present STEPSIC, an open-source initial condition generator for cosmological N-body simulations in the periodic cuboid, spherical, and cylindrical geometries supported by StePS. It succeeds the earlier StePS initial condition code and extends it to periodic cuboids with arbitrary aspect ratios and cylindrical topologies. Gaussian density fields are generated on a periodic Fourier grid. First- and second-order Lagrangian perturbation theory (LPT) displacements and velocities are interpolated to lattices or relaxed glasses with radially varying particle masses. For spherical and cylindrical domains, an enclosing periodic box supplies the fields, and a multiresolution scheme matches resolved wavelengths to local particle mass. With identical white noise, the periodic calculation agrees with monofonIC to within $0.05\%$ in power spectrum and $0.15\%$ in median particle displacement. On relaxed spherical and cylindrical glasses, comparison with independent sums over retained Fourier modes gives errors consistent with linear interpolation. For an enclosing box of one domain diameter, the root-mean-square relative displacement of two points in the high-resolution region differs from the infinite-Universe value by at most $0.0014\,h^{-1}\mathrm{Mpc}$ out of $0.5\,h^{-1}\mathrm{Mpc}$ at $z=31$, while domain-scale mean-density variance is suppressed. In one cylindrical realization evolved to $z=0$, doubling the enclosing box shifts the high-resolution region by $0.39\,h^{-1}\mathrm{Mpc}$; after removing this bulk displacement, power spectra differ by at most $1.05\%$. In a cylindrical StePS simulation evolved to $z=0$, first-order initial conditions leave up to $3.6\%$ less nonlinear power than second-order ones, consistent with LPT transients.

arxiv.org/abs/2605.11193.title: Prospects for multi-messenger discovery of the gravitational-wave background anisotropies via cross-correlation with galaxies
arxiv.org/abs/2605.11193.excerpt:
arXiv:2605.11193v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present new empirically grounded forecasts for the observability of stochastic gravitational-wave background anisotropies assuming a population of stellar-mass compact binary coalescences as its source. We quantified the discovery potential using simulations based on the Euclid Flagship Galaxy Catalogue and LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA observational constraints in combination with detailed theoretical modelling. We considered the multi-messenger cross-correlation with galaxies as well as the gravitational wave-only cross-correlation across observation-time bins. We found that signal-to-noise ratio greater than five is achievable via cross-correlation of a galaxy catalogue that is complete up to limiting magnitude $i < 24.7$ and has redshift uncertainties $\sigma_z = 0.003 (1+z)$ with a gravitational-wave sky map corresponding to 2 years of observation by a third-generation detector network comprising three interferometers. Network configurations with LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA plus up to two third-generation detectors would be limited to moderate signal-to-noise levels, between three and five, except if merger rates are near the upper bound set by observational constraints, in which case the threshold of five would be reached after 4 years. Detectability without the multi-messenger tracer has proven significantly more challenging, with signal-to-noise ratio remaining below three after 10 years. In light of the plans being carried out in the community for ongoing and upcoming galaxy surveys, this work bodes well for the multi-messenger discovery and exploration of the stochastic gravitational-wave background in the era of next-generation observatories such as the Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.09690.title: Stochastic constant-roll inflation beyond the hilltop with the spectral method
arxiv.org/abs/2606.09690.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.09690v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Stochastic inflation can be used to study large inflationary perturbations. This paper presents such a study for a quadratic hilltop potential, corresponding to constant-roll inflation. I solve the perturbation distribution using the spectral method, with detailed solutions of the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of the Fokker-Planck operator. Contrary to previous studies of stochastic constant-roll inflation, the solution allows trajectories that cross the hilltop and get stuck near a reflecting boundary on the other side, tunneling out slowly in a way dictated by the lowest eigensolution. Despite their rarity, these trajectories turn out to dominate the mean first-passage time. For this reason, I argue the mean does not properly describe the inflationary background. Using the median instead, I compute the distribution of the coarse-grained $\Delta N$ distribution and show that its well-known exponential tail first flattens out and then forms a peak near a maximal $\Delta N$ value. I argue similar intricacies arise in primordial black hole models.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.08835.title: Hybrid Simulations of Proton Acceleration at Oblique High-$\beta$ Shocks
arxiv.org/abs/2607.08835.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.08835v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Collisionless shocks in the intracluster and intergalactic medium (ICM/IGM) are expected to energize both electrons and ions. While electron acceleration is revealed by prominent radio emission, $\gamma$-ray emission from hadronic interactions remains undetected, suggesting that high-$\beta$ (ratio of thermal to magnetic pressure), low-Mach-number shocks cannot accelerate protons efficiently. We present three-dimensional hybrid simulations of quasi-perpendicular shocks with sonic Mach numbers $M_s\sim{3.4{-}17.5}$, focusing primarily on high-$\beta$ conditions representative of cluster environments and including several lower-$\beta$ comparison runs. We find that weak shocks with $M_s\lesssim5$ are consistently inefficient, with $\varepsilon_{\rm CR}\lesssim0.1\%$, while inefficient cases can persist to substantially higher $M_s$ depending on $M_A$ and $\beta$. In contrast, stronger shocks ($M_s \gtrsim 10$) develop clear power-law tails with slopes $q \sim 4.0$ and reach $\varepsilon_{\rm CR} \sim 3\%$. These results suggest that weak, oblique ICM shocks are generally unlikely to accelerate protons efficiently. However, reducing $\vartheta_{B_n}$ to $\sim 45^\circ$ leads to substantially higher acceleration efficiencies, indicating that magnetic obliquity plays a critical role in determining proton acceleration. Our findings provide a microphysical framework for interpreting radio relic observations, whose polarization suggests that electrons are accelerated at oblique shocks, and the absence of cluster $\gamma$-ray detections.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.09109.title: Fast Radio Bursts Trace Cosmic Star Formation with Little Delay
arxiv.org/abs/2607.09109.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.09109v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The progenitor channels of fast radio bursts (FRBs) remain debated, with a central question being whether their cosmic rate traces star formation promptly or instead follows it with the long time-delay characteristic of compact-binary mergers. We perform a forward-modeling, hierarchical Bayesian analysis of the CHIME/FRB population, jointly fitting the catalog sample, baseband fluences, and localized host redshifts, while self-consistently incorporating the survey selection function through the injection framework. Adopting the classical cosmic star formation history (SFH) with a range of delay-time models, we find that the reconstructed FRB rate robustly tracks the SFH peak. All models exclude characteristic delays $\Delta t_d > 1.0$ Gyr at the 90\% credible level, with inferred median peak offsets in the range $\Delta t_d = 0.1$--$0.3$ Gyr that remain consistent with a prompt, zero-delay origin at the 2$\sigma$ level. This finding disfavors the previously reported multi-Gyr delays, strongly indicating that the central engine is linked to young remnants (likely magnetars) from stellar collapse and, potentially, to the prompt merger of compact objects.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.10282.title: A UV-to-Near-infrared QSO Composite Spectrum from the SPHEREx All-Sky Survey
arxiv.org/abs/2607.10282.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.10282v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present a composite spectrum of $\sim 61,000$ type 1 SDSS QSOs (median $z \approx 1.26$), constructed using SPHEREx spectrophotometric data and covering a rest-frame wavelength range of $0.14-4.5~\mu$m. The SPHEREx mission surveys the entire sky in 102 near-infrared spectral channels spanning $0.75-5.0~\mu$m with a spectral resolution of $R \approx 35-130$, providing a unique dataset for building a statistically robust QSO composite. We find that the UV and optical continuum of the resulting composite can be described by a power law, $f_
u \propto 
u^{\alpha_
u}$, with a best-fit spectral index of $\alpha_
u = -0.10$, while the near-infrared continuum is well-fit with a spectral index of $-1.46$. The power-law indices in both the optical and near-infrared regimes strongly depend on properties of QSOs, such that more luminous QSOs tend to exhibit flatter UV/optical and steeper near-infrared continua compared to those of less luminous ones. The IR-to-optical flux ratio decreases with increasing AGN luminosity, consistent with the predictions of the receding torus model. The line ratios of broad emission lines, including H$\alpha$, Pa$ eta$, and Pa$\alpha$, are in good agreement with predictions from Case B recombination, suggesting that internal extinction is almost negligible. The equivalent widths of these emission lines are proportional to AGN luminosity, contrary to the trend expected from the Baldwin effect. Finally, the shape of the composite is sensitive to host-galaxy contamination, which must be considered when utilizing this QSO composite for subsequent scientific applications.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.11438.title: Direct Primary Beam Correction: A Regularised Linear Operator for Untangling Mutual Coupling in SKA-Low 21-cm Cosmology
arxiv.org/abs/2607.11438.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.11438v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Mutual coupling has emerged as the dominant direction-dependent corruption in dense aperture arrays, imprinting spatial and sub-MHz spectral structure that compromises time-gating and foreground-removal strategies. We introduce \textit{direct primary beam correction}, a domain-agnostic, regularised, direction-weighted linear inversion of stacked Jones matrices that transforms an aperture array's far-field pattern towards an arbitrary target. Using full-wave electromagnetic simulations of SKA-Low and a 4-hour observation of the EoR0 field spanning 122--134~MHz, we show that the correction reproduces the target pattern exactly for as many directions as there are elements, with regularisation trading in-field accuracy for sidelobe conditioning. For 21-cm power-spectrum analysis, we introduce a cross-time estimator that correlates samples within each $uv$ cell only between different time blocks. As the field is tracked, sidelobe emission decorrelates between blocks, suppressing its coupling-induced leakage into the EoR window; however, the main beam's coupling-induced chromaticity remains coherent and biases the recovered power, a bias that longer integration does not remove. Combined with the correction, the estimator recovers the input power without bias and passes a foreground-only null test, trading the systematic bias for statistical scatter that averages down over independent correction cycles. Propagating Gaussian beam-model errors shows that detection requires embedded element patterns accurate to at least 3.25 significant figures for channel-independent errors. In contrast, common approximations, such as averaged or neighbouring-channel patterns, reach at most two. Mutual coupling is therefore correctable in principle, making beam characterisation, rather than the correction, the priority for 21-cm experiments with dense aperture arrays.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.16405.title: The Goldstone Awakens: Unimodular dark energy in scale-invariant $R^2$ gravity
arxiv.org/abs/2607.16405.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.16405v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We construct an $R^2$ cosmology based on scale invariance and unimodular gravity in which the Goldstone boson of dilatations establishes a predictive connection between inflation and dark energy. The conservation of the corresponding Noether current confines the inflationary trajectory to a one-dimensional orbit in field space, freezing the Goldstone direction and rendering the inflationary dynamics effectively single field. After inflation, the system settles on a Minkowski vacuum manifold. The unimodular integration constant, already present in the full theory but negligible during inflation, lifts the flat Goldstone direction, generating an exponential potential for the canonically normalised field. Unlike in phenomenological quintessence models, its slope is not a free DE parameter, but is instead fixed by the field-space geometry inherited from the inflationary attractor. This geometry excludes matter-era tracking and, throughout the inflationary viability region, places the field in the thawing regime compatible with accelerated expansion. For a representative inflationary benchmark, the now pseudo-Goldstone field remains frozen until close to the present epoch, yielding DE equation-of-state parameters $(w_0,w_a)\simeq(-0.992,-0.011)$ in the CPL parametrisation $w(a)=w_0+w_a(1-a)$. More generally, the same parameter controlling the inflationary spectral tilt also fixes the slope of the DE potential, leading to a tight correlation between early- and late-Universe observables: increasing the thawing signal lowers $n_s$, while values of $n_s$ closer to unity drive the model towards $\Lambda$CDM.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.17929.title: gevolution 2.0: GPU-accelerated relativistic N-body simulations for cosmology
arxiv.org/abs/2607.17929.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.17929v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: High-performance computing is increasingly dominated by hardware acceleration using Graphics Processing Units (GPUs). To take advantage of this long-term trend, we implement a major overhaul of the parallelisation approach in the relativistic particle-mesh N-body code gevolution. The new version 2.0 of gevolution employs three layers of parallelisation: MPI for scalability on a distributed memory system, shared memory parallelisation on each MPI rank using OpenMP, and offloading all compute intensive tasks to GPUs using CUDA. The code also includes many new features that have been developed over the past years. We provide an overview of the code structure and show key performance benchmarks. This publication is accompanied by the simultaneous public release of gevolution 2.0 and of a GPU-ready version of the LATfield2 library which provides the parallelisation backend.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.25317.title: Gravitational Waves from Superconducting Cosmic Strings
arxiv.org/abs/2607.25317.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.25317v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We study the evolution of superconducting cosmic-string networks in a $U(1)_{\rm local}\times U(1)_{\rm global}$ field-theoretic model using three-dimensional lattice field simulations in an expanding universe. The scalar field charged under $U(1)_{\rm local}$ forms cosmic strings, while the scalar field associated with $U(1)_{\rm global}$ acts as a current carrier and condenses in their vicinity. We investigate the evolution of the string network for several values of the coupling constant between the string-forming and current-carrier fields and estimate the gravitational-wave power spectrum sourced by the resulting superconducting cosmic-string network. We find that the spectral shape depends on the coupling constant: as the interaction strength increases, the spectrum is suppressed on small scales. This feature may be probed by future high-frequency gravitational-wave observations.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.28919.title: Strongly Magnetized Super-Eddington Accretion: How Spin and Accretion Rate Regulate Energy Output and Mass Loss
arxiv.org/abs/2607.28919.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.28919v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Strongly magnetized super-Eddington accretion flows power many important astrophysical systems, but how black hole parameters control their output is unclear. We present 30 general relativistic radiation magnetohydrodynamics simulations of super-Eddington magnetically arrested disks onto stellar-mass black holes, varying mass ($M_{\rm BH}= 5, 15, 30\,M_{\odot}$), spin ($a=0.0,0.9$), and accretion rate ($\dot{M}_{\rm acc} \approx 1-2000\,\dot{M}_{\rm Edd}$). We find that black hole spin and accretion rate jointly regulate wind loss rates and energy output efficiencies, while black hole mass has no effect over the mass range studied here. The BH accretes only $7-30\%$ of the mass supplied to the accretion flow, while the rest is expelled in winds. This accretion fraction decreases with mass supply rate and is lower for high-spin systems. Both spin states produce strong magnetically driven outflows. For $a = 0$, the wind kinetic, radiative, and electromagnetic efficiencies are modest and show little variation across the full simulated range of accretion rates. For $a = 0.9$, both wind power and jet power increase super-linearly with $\dot{M}_{\rm acc}$, with the jet power saturating beyond $\dot{M}_{\rm acc} \sim 100\,\dot{M}_{\rm Edd}$. Radiation is strongly beamed along the funnel, with inverse beaming factors exceeding $100$ for high-spin, high-$\dot{m}$ models viewed face-on. Our results establish that rapid BH spin boosts energy-extraction efficiency, while high accretion rate amplifies total power. We provide scaling relations for luminosities, jet power, accretion ratio, and beaming, offering a framework for interpreting observations of ULXs and other super-Eddington systems.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.10451.title: JWST Spectroscopy of Type Ia Supernova 2025rbs from Maximum Light to the Nebular Phase
arxiv.org/abs/2608.10451.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.10451v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present JWST observations of the Type Ia supernova (SN Ia) 2025rbs ($D=$14.5 Mpc) at +1, +23, and +84 days after B-band maximum, spanning a wavelength-dependent transition toward the nebular phase. Combined with ground-based optical and near-infrared (NIR) data, our panchromatic spectra (0.4-14 $\mu$m) include the first maximum-light mid-infrared (MIR) spectrum and the earliest MIR spectroscopic sequence of an SN Ia to date. At peak light, the MIR spectrum exhibits a continuum with permitted and forbidden features, including Si II, Ni II, Mg II, and early-emerging [Ni III-IV] and [Ar II-III]. By +23 days the MIR is dominated by forbidden lines with a weak continuum, and by +84 days it is fully nebular, whereas the optical/NIR spectra remain transitional. The nebular spectrum reveals strongly stratified ejecta, with stable Ni concentrated at the lowest velocities, radioactive Co at intermediate velocities but absent within ~2000 km s$^{-1}$, and Ar occupying an outer shell. We detect small-scale substructure in [Ca IV] 3.21 $\mu$m with few-percent amplitudes on a characteristic scale of ~800 km s$^{-1}$, reflecting clumping in composition or ionization. Radiative-transfer calculations at +1 day substantially underpredict the MIR Mg II features (4.6, 9.6, and 13.0 $\mu$m) despite approximately reproducing the NIR Mg II 1.0927 $\mu$m line, suggesting that the relative strengths of the NIR and MIR transitions are sensitive to the treatment of Mg ionization and excitation. These observations demonstrate that MIR spectroscopy beginning near maximum light simultaneously probes the emerging inner ejecta and rapidly fading outer burning products, providing new constraints for explosion and radiative-transfer models.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.16275.title: Multipolar neutrino radiation in binary neutron star mergers: Angular structure, rotational variability, and implications for electron fraction
arxiv.org/abs/2608.16275.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.16275v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The angular structure and temporal variability of neutrino emission from binary neutron star mergers are characterized using fully general-relativistic simulations with energy-integrated M1 neutrino transport across a representative set of equations of state, total masses and mass ratios. The main analysis is restricted to merger remnants that do not collapse to a black hole within the simulated time intervals. The angle-dependent neutrino energy flux is extracted on a spherical surface outside the remnant and decomposed into spherical harmonics to quantify its multipolar content and evolution. Following the initial post-merger transient, the neutrino radiation flux approaches an axisymmetric configuration dominated by a strong quadrupolar component, producing persistent polar flux enhancement and equatorial suppression due to torus shadowing. The dipolar contribution remains subdominant, indicating the absence of sustained one-sided emission. The degree of anisotropy increases with mass asymmetry and for softer equations of state, reflecting the compactness and morphology of the remnant--disk system. Superimposed on this time-averaged geometry, coherent azimuthal modulations associated with the $m=1$ mode are identified. The associated half frequency, $f_{\mathrm{dom}}/2\simeq0.6$--$0.7\,\mathrm{kHz}$, is compared with local rotation rates in the simulated remnant--disk systems, suggesting a possible dynamical association between the remnant structure and neutrino variability. Finally, we quantify how the same quadrupole-dominated radiation geometry induces a latitude-dependent equilibrium electron fraction. The polar material is driven close to the neutrino-equilibrium target, whereas equatorial material remains systematically more neutron rich and below equilibrium.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.23367.title: Black holes from a Higgs-like field in the radiation era
arxiv.org/abs/2608.23367.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.23367v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Light spectator fields during inflation can acquire superhorizon fluctuations that cross a potential barrier between positive and negative regions of their potential. Motivated by the Standard Model Higgs instability, in this work we study the subsequent evolution of patches where this occurs in the radiation era after inflation ends for a Higgs-like spectator field. We utilise fully nonlinear, spherically symmetric numerical relativity. Across the black hole forming configurations in our investigation we find a robust two-stage evolution. First, the central negative potential region reverses its expansion, becomes kinetic dominated, and forms a primordial black hole that hides the runaway core. The positive potential barrier that survives outside this first horizon then determines one of two late-time branches. In the subcritical branch the original apparent horizon grows smoothly and engulfs the remaining scalar structure. In the supercritical branch, however, the potential energy of the barrier dominates the local evolution. The result is a transient wormhole throat, a bifurcating trapping horizon, and an inflating child universe branch. In both branches the parent radiation dominated universe is ultimately left with an ordinary primordial black hole whose subsequent growth is governed by radiation accretion.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.10319.title: Extending the Little Red Dot population at intermediate redshift with VIPERS
arxiv.org/abs/2609.10319.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.10319v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Little red dots (LRDs) are a recently identified population of compact, red sources characterised by a distinctive V-shaped UV-to-optical continuum and broad emission lines. Their physical structure and evolution remain uncertain, while their properties at intermediate redshifts are largely unexplored. We identify and characterise LRD-like sources at 0.5<1.75 using the VIMOS Public Extragalactic Redshift Survey (VIPERS), extending observational studies to a previously poorly explored cosmic epoch. We select candidates from their UV and optical slopes measured from broadband photometry and refine the sample using broad emission lines in VIPERS spectroscopy. We investigate their photometric, spectroscopic, and morphological properties, constrain their physical sizes with HSC imaging, measure their comoving number density and evolution, and characterise their local environments using the VIPERS galaxy density field. We also model the multi-wavelength emission of the unique X-ray-detected source with CIGALE, including X-ray and AGN emission. We identify 14 LRD-like sources, including one X-ray-detected object, whose HSC morphology remains unresolved. We measure their number density in two redshift bins, 0.5<1 and 1<1.75, and combine our results with literature measurements. We find a rapid decline in number density after cosmic noon. The two sources with sufficiently constrained environments are located in underdense regions. The SED of the X-ray-detected source is best reproduced by a radiatively efficient accretion disk viewed at low inclination. Our results demonstrate that LRD-like sources are present at z>0.5, bridging local and high-redshift studies. Their abundance, compact morphology, environmental properties, and multi-wavelength emission provide new constraints on the evolution and physical origin of this population.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.11102.title: The Binary Fraction of Milky Way Field Stars in DESI: Dependence on Chemical Abundances
arxiv.org/abs/2610.11102.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.11102v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Binary populations encode information about the physical conditions of star formation and the subsequent evolution of stellar populations. Adopting a statistical method based on multi-epoch line-of-sight velocity variations, we constrain the binary fraction, $f_b$, of field main-sequence turn-off stars in the Milky Way using data from the second data release of the DESI Milky Way Survey. Our measurements are mainly sensitive to binaries with orbital periods shorter than approximately $10^4$ days. The inferred total binary fractions account statistically for less detectable systems through forward modeling under an assumed orbital-period distribution. $f_b$ is found to primarily increase with lower [Fe/H]. At $[\mathrm{Fe}/\mathrm{H}]\gtrsim -1.3$, $f_b$ shows a modest increase with increasing [Mg/Fe], whereas no clear trend is detected at lower [Fe/H]. The apparent variations of $f_b$ with angular momentum and Galactic height are largely explained by their underlying [Fe/H] distributions, while the remaining variations broadly follow differences in [Mg/Fe]. Within overlapping regions of the [Fe/H]--[Mg/Fe] plane, the thin disk, thick disk, stellar halo and GSE populations exhibit no significant differences in their binary fractions. Thus, our measurements indicate that the variation in $f_b$ is dominated by chemical abundance, which could be explained by the metallicity-dependent gas cooling efficiency and fragmentation. The weaker [Mg/Fe] dependence at fixed [Fe/H] might be associated with the formation conditions of stars, with higher [Mg/Fe] stars generally forming earlier under a more gas-rich and turbulent environment.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.21722.title: Hydrostatic Equilibrium Estimate of the Fuzzy Dark Matter Mass from Dwarf Spheroidals: Method and Systematics
arxiv.org/abs/2610.21722.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.21722v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present an estimator of an effective fuzzy (wave) dark matter (FDM) boson mass based on local hydrostatic equilibrium, which requires no soliton or other parametric density template. The condition requires the classical gravitational acceleration to be balanced by the gradient of the quantum potential in the Schr\"odinger--Poisson--Madelung system. We apply it to the density and enclosed-mass posteriors of nine Milky Way dwarf spheroidal (dSph) galaxies obtained with \textsc{pyGravSphere}. For each posterior realization, we determine by least squares the boson mass that best satisfies the force-balance condition over a fixed radial window. This gives a distribution of \(m_{21}\equiv m/10^{-21}\,\mathrm{eV}\) for each galaxy. The per-galaxy median masses range from \(m_{21}\sim 8\) to \(46\), corresponding to \(m\sim(0.8\text{--}4.6)\times10^{-20}\,\mathrm{eV}\); Draco and Ursa Minor have the lowest median masses, while Carina and Sextans have the highest. The inverse-variance-weighted effective equilibrium mass of the nine galaxies is \(m=(1.31\pm0.35)\times10^{-20}\,\mathrm{eV}\), with Draco and Ursa Minor contributing most of the weight. We also examine the systematic uncertainties in our results.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.28728.title: Exploring the origin of slow-rotating pulsars: Emission from STARS simulated white dwarfs
arxiv.org/abs/2610.28728.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.28728v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: An increasing number of slow-rotating pulsars and long-period transients have been observed in recent years. The periods of these sources can be significantly longer than typical pulsar sources, ranging from ~ 100 - 1000 s, or even longer. The observed periods and period derivatives predict high magnetic fields, higher than the Schwinger field, when we consider conventional pulsar models of dipole-driven emission from neutron stars. Interestingly, the periods of these sources are consistent with the current observations of white dwarfs (WDs). We explore the possibility of magnetic WDs, simulated using the stellar evolution code STARS, as the origin of some of these unusual pulsar observations. We simulate WDs with enhanced magnetic fields due to accretion after their formation. We also briefly touch on the more exotic possibility of super-Chandrasekhar WDs as the origin for these sources. We find that expanding the parameter space to include the possibility of a WD origin provides an alternate and viable explanation for these unusual observations.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.40550.title: An Empirically Calibrated [C II] Luminosity-Halo Mass Relation for Line Intensity Mapping
arxiv.org/abs/2610.40550.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.40550v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Millimeter-wave line intensity mapping (LIM) aims to observe the high-redshift universe through the 158 $\mu$m fine-structure line of [C II], the brightest far-infrared line of star-forming galaxies. Whether the clustering of large-scale structure, which carries rich cosmological information, is measurable in the [C II] signal at $z>4$ or buried under the shot noise of the emitters is determined from the amplitude and shape of the [C II] power spectrum. We calibrate $L(M_h,z)$ on [C II] data alone: the mean [C II] intensity from tomographic cross-correlation at $0<4.2$ and the luminosity-function measurements and limits at $z\simeq0$ and $4.3\lesssim z\lesssim8$. We model the relation as a double power law and fit its four parameters at $z=4.5$ and 5.5 separately, with no assumption about their evolution, and then jointly across $0<7$, and we examine how the uncertainty depends on the modeling assumptions. The shape of the power spectrum is settled by the existing data. The clustering peak stands a factor of $45\,(23-93)$ and $64\,(38-112)$ above the shot-noise floor at $z=4.5$ and 5.5, and the two cross at $k_c\simeq 0.37$ and 0.44 $h$ Mpc$^{-1}$. The amplitude is known less well, the clustering power to $0.5-0.6$ dex and the shot noise to $0.7-0.9$ dex. The luminosity-weighted bias, which together with the mean intensity sets the clustering amplitude, is known to about 10\% within the assumptions of this work and is relatively high, about 4. The results show that the signal comes from halos of $10^{11}-10^{12}\,M_\odot$, similar in mass to the hosts of the Lyman-break galaxies and Ly$\alpha$ emitters that galaxy surveys map at these redshifts.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.06916.title: ReveaLLAGN 3: Revealing the Infrared Spectral Energy Distributions of Low Luminosity AGN
arxiv.org/abs/2611.06916.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.06916v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The spectral energy distributions of active galactic nuclei (AGN) provide valuable information on the emission mechanisms taking place in their inner regions. Here we use the James Webb Space Telescope to study the near and mid-infrared spectral energy distributions of seven nearby low-luminosity active galaxy nuclei from 1.7 to 24 $\mu m$. We cleanly separate the AGN spectrum by performing spatial fits of the two-dimensional images across all wavelengths. We then compare these clean unresolved spectra to aperture-based spectra and show that they effectively remove galaxy contamination. Comparing our infrared measurements to X-ray emission, we find that low-luminosity AGN have enhanced near-infrared emission relative to more luminous AGN, a trend that correlates with radio-loudness, while their mid-infrared-to-X-ray ratios are comparable. A majority of our targets show strong compact silicate emission suggesting the presence of warm dust on parsec scales in these systems. We also quantify the near- and mid-infrared power-law slopes and colors of low-luminosity AGN. In the near-infrared we find AGN of all luminosities have similar spectral slopes and colors, however in the mid-infrared, we find low-luminosity AGN typically have steeper slopes and redder colors than more luminous AGN. Both the strong silicate emission and steep mid-infrared slopes disagree with existing models for low-luminosity AGN spectral energy distributions.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.12556.title: BAO and Type Ia Supernovae in LTB Cosmology: Constraints on Radial Inhomogeneity and Acoustic-Ruler Evolution
arxiv.org/abs/2611.12556.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.12556v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We investigate how baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) and Type Ia supernovae constrain radial density profiles and acoustic-ruler evolution in Lema\^itre-Tolman-Bondi (LTB) cosmology with a cosmological constant. A consistent extension of a homogeneous analysis requires modified distances and unequal radial and transverse ruler stretching. Transverse BAO and supernovae isolate ruler evolution without fixing its absolute length. We connect this test to exact nonlinear, compensated density profiles with free depth, width, shell location and exterior matter density, keeping the observer at the symmetry centre. We fit DESI DR2 BAO and DES-Dovekie supernovae with full covariances and matched calibration freedom in LTB and flat $\Lambda$CDM. Conditional on evaluating BAO predictions at effective redshifts, LTB improves the full-sample $\chi^2$ by 8.5 with three additional parameters. DESI rejects the specific deep profile preferred without it, while distinct profiles remain nearly degenerate. Selecting DES supernovae alone gives a shallower shell and a gain of 7.44, almost entirely from BAO and unchanged by an additional magnitude-uncertainty cut. Two illustrative redshift-window tests retain a DES-only gain close to 7 at this geometry. The preferred profile and ruler history depend on the supernova selection. The full-sample gain occurs in at least 7% of simulated flat-$\Lambda$CDM data sets and does not establish an inhomogeneity detection; this calibration is not transferred to DES-only fits. Small finite-ruler corrections do not validate survey-bin averaging. In the local approximation, common LTB ruler evolution shifts angular and transverse three-dimensional BAO together and cannot by itself explain their discrepancy.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.14635.title: FRIDA: Finding Rotation In ultra-Diffuse gAlaxies. I. Programme overview, resolved gas density profiles, and HI mass-size relation
arxiv.org/abs/2611.14635.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.14635v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Gas-rich ultra-diffuse galaxies (UDGs) provide powerful tests of galaxy formation models at low surface densities. However, the structure of their neutral atomic hydrogen (HI) remains poorly constrained, hampering our understanding of this population.
  We present FRIDA (Finding Rotation In ultra-Diffuse gAlaxies), a MeerKAT and VLA programme providing high-resolution HI data of 12 gas-rich UDGs. In this paper, we introduce our sample and delve into the associated observations and data reduction. We derive HI fluxes, masses ($M_{\rm HI}$), and resolved surface density profiles ($\Sigma_{\rm HI}(R)$). We find extended ($\sim 7-30\ \rm{kpc}$ in radius) and regular HI emission in our UDGs, and we report the discovery of a satellite around one of them. Moreover, we place our UDGs in the $M_{\rm HI}-R_{\rm HI}$ and $M_{\rm HI}-R_{\rm 50,HI}$ mass-size relations, where $R_{\rm HI}$ is radius at which $\Sigma_{\rm HI}(R)=1\ M_\odot \rm{pc^{-2}}$, and $R_{\rm 50,HI}$ is the radius enclosing $50\%$ of $M_{\rm HI}$. While our UDGs lie within the scatter of the relations, they systematically fall on their upper side, being slightly (by $\sim 15-25\%$) more extended and of lower mean $\Sigma_{\rm HI}$ (by $\sim 25-35\%$) than average galaxies at similar $M_{\rm HI}$.
