Approximately one Earth mass of gas reaching Sagittarius A every decade could sustain its current activity level.

mars_quake_fault_location.headline: Marsquake Linked to Deep Fault Beneath Valles Marineris Canyon
mars_quake_fault_location.summary: A marsquake recorded by InSight (S0976a) has been traced to a 20‑40 km deep fault beneath Valles Marineris, suggesting recent tectonic activity.
highlights: The quake S0976a was detected on sol 976 of the InSight mission, the farthest event recorded to date.
Source modeling places the fault 20–40 km beneath the canyon, comparable to Earth’s New Madrid Seismic Zone.
The finding supports earlier hypotheses of a strike‑slip fault beneath Valles Marineris from Mars Odyssey and MRO data.

arxiv_2611_25036v1.headline: Simulation-based inference sharpens reconstruction of electroweak gravitational-wave signals
arxiv_2611_25036v1.summary: A likelihood‑free simulation‑based inference method accurately recovers electroweak phase‑transition parameters from stochastic gravitational‑wave backgrounds, matching traditional MCMC results.
highlights: SBI delivers reliable parameter posteriors for the SGWB despite degeneracies in the model‑to‑spectrum mapping
The method reproduces results of a full likelihood Markov chain Monte Carlo analysis with negligible per‑data‑set cost
Applied to a singlet extension of the Standard Model, SBI reconstructs the transition strength, inverse duration, temperature
Importance sampling using the SBI posterior improves sampling efficiency by several orders of magnitude over prior sampling

elnino_2026_unprecedented.institution: Various climate research institutions (e.g., NOAA, climate modeling centers)
elnino_2026_unprecedented.headline: 2026 El Niño Sets Record Heat, Fuels Extreme Pacific Hurricanes
elnino_2026_unprecedented.summary: In 2026, El Niño reached unprecedented sea surface temperatures above 30 °C, driving the strongest Pacific hurricane season and global climate disruptions.
highlights: Average sea surface temperature in the central‑eastern Pacific exceeded 30 °C (86 °F) for the first time on record.
September’s daily average was 3.03 °C above the 30‑year mean, with WMO projecting a possible 3.7 °C anomaly by January.
Cyclone energy accumulated to 331 units by mid‑October, surpassing the previous record of 318 units set in 2018.
The intense El Niño suppressed Atlantic hurricane activity while intensifying Pacific storms.

sunspot_sound_wave_jets.headline: Sound Waves Trigger Fiery Plasma Jets From Sunspot Penumbra
sunspot_sound_wave_jets.summary: Around 176 dynamic fibrils were tracked erupting at 16 km s⁻¹ from sunspot NOAA 13182, linking magnetoacoustic shocks to coronal heating.
highlights: 176 jets observed over one hour on 10 Jan 2023 using NVST, CHASE and SDO.
Jets rise at ~16 km s⁻¹, reach ~1,130 km, and fall back after ~4.5 min.
Their cadence matches the five‑minute running penumbral waves, indicating magnetoacoustic shock driving.
Magnetic field tilt controls deceleration and pulse interval of the fibrils.

after_8_years_in_space_a_groundbreaking_.headline: MIXS X‑ray Telescope Achieves First Light After 8‑Year Journey
after_8_years_in_space_a_groundbreaking_.summary: After eight years and 10 billion km in space, the Mercury Imaging X‑ray Spectrometer captured its first cosmic X‑ray data, exceeding expectations.
highlights: MIXS observed the Crab Nebula for 55 orientations over 39 hours, confirming sharper angular resolution than its 2015 ground tests
No radiation damage or stray‑light effects were detected, and only minor self‑fluorescence remains to be calibrated
The instrument’s performance paves the way for detailed elemental mapping of Mercury’s surface during BepiColombo’s science phase

stellar_merger_andromeda.headline: James Webb Captures First Real‑Time Stellar Merger in Andromeda
stellar_merger_andromeda.summary: Astronomers observed a supergiant swallowing its smaller companion in the Andromeda galaxy, tracking the merger from onset to completion over seven years.
highlights: The binary system AT 2025abao (named Bao) was first flagged by NASA’s retired NEOWISE mission in 2023.
JWST infrared imaging in December 2025 revealed rapid common‑envelope evolution as the smaller star plunged into the
The merger unfolded in under seven years, far faster than theoretical models had predicted.
Future monitoring with the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will test whether Bao’s rejuvenated star remains stable.

evolution_mutation_rate_challenge.headline: Decades‑Old Theory That Essential Genes Avoid Mutations Refuted
evolution_mutation_rate_challenge.summary: A comprehensive analysis of spontaneous mutations in Escherichia coli and Saccharomyces cerevisiae finds no link between gene essentiality and lower mutation rates.
highlights: Analyzed the largest dataset of spontaneous mutations to date across bacteria and yeast.
Found no correlation between gene essentiality and mutation frequency in either species.
Identified genome‑structural factors, not gene importance, as drivers of mutation rate variation.

humandna_mouse_2026.headline: Human DNA Chunk Inserted into Mice Reveals Glial Role in XDP
humandna_mouse_2026.summary: Researchers used the SwAP-In technique to insert 78,000 human DNA letters into mice, uncovering glial cell involvement in the rare XDP disorder.
highlights: SwAP-In enabled insertion of a human TAF1 segment and its jumping gene into mouse embryonic stem cells.
XDP mice displayed rapid symptom onset within 1.5 months, accelerating therapeutic testing.
Oligodendrocyte numbers and myelin production were dramatically reduced in the striatum of XDP mice.
Boosting TAF1 expression rescued protein levels in cultured mouse cells, suggesting a potential treatment avenue.

human_family_tree_revision.headline: Monash Study Calls for Radical Rewrite of Human Family Tree
human_family_tree_revision.summary: New research argues that Australopithecus and Paranthropus should be reclassified within the genus Homo, reshaping five million years of human evolution.
highlights: The proposal, published in American Journal of Biological Anthropology, suggests expanding Homo to include Australopithecus and
Lead author Dr. Ian Towle of Monash Biomedicine Discovery Institute argues that traditional taxonomic boundaries no longer
Recent discoveries show brain size and tool use are unreliable markers for separating ancient hominin groups.
Reclassifying these species could provide a more stable taxonomy for the past 4‑5 million years of evolution.

evt_289d976d4e.headline: Nano-sandwich photocathode improves solar conversion of CO₂ into ethanol

evt_17daa6a3ee.headline: The universe is still speeding up, but nobody knows why

evt_e79b64b01a.headline: Galápagos corals show El Niño events are more extreme now than in past 1,000 years

evt_1126200f2f.headline: Free-falling atoms in space put a new twist on Galileo’s gravity test

evt_a209c81e80.headline: Scientists discover why damaged nerves struggle to heal

evt_87762b8fc8.headline: Dogs may hold surprising clues to human longevity
